Title: Three men nabbed in cable theft attempt in Taman Seri Sentosa
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Three men were arrested after police found them inside a utility manhole during an operation to investigate an attempted cable theft in Taman Seri Sentosa here yesterday.
The arrests followed a viral video on Threads showing one of the suspects being detained inside a manhole along Jalan Seri Sentosa.
Brickfields police chief Assistant Commissioner Hoo Chang Hook said the operation began at 4pm after police received public information about suspicious activities at the location.
"A team from the Petaling police station task force, assisted by other police personnel, inspected the location and found two men inside the utility manhole.
"Both men were arrested, and police seized eight items, including cable cutters and an electric-powered cable pulling device, to facilitate investigations," he said in a statement today.
Hoo said police returned to the location at 7.30pm for further checks.
"With assistance from the Fire and Rescue Department and Telekom Malaysia, water was pumped out of the manhole.
"Police then discovered another man inside and arrested him," he said.
All three suspects and the seized equipment were taken to the Petaling police station for further action.
Hoo said the case was being investigated under Section 379, read together with Section 511 of the Penal Code, for attempted theft.
Investigations are ongoing to determine each suspect's role, verify ownership of the cables and establish whether any damage or financial losses were incurred.
He thanked members of the public for providing information that led to the arrests.
Those with information on the case can contact Brickfields police at 03-22979222 or visit the nearest police station.

Title: Make health insurance mandatory for UNHCR-registered refugees, govt urged
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government should require all refugees registered with the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) to have health insurance, to ease the financial burden on public healthcare facilities.
Datuk Dr Mohd Radzi Md Jidin (PN-Putrajaya) said UNHCR should take responsibility for refugees issued with its cards by ensuring they were insured when seeking treatment at government hospitals and clinics.
"If they are so clever at giving out cards and allowing them in, then take responsibility and provide insurance," he said when debating the Health Ministry's allocation under the Supply Bill 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Radzi cited a written parliamentary reply from Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail yesterday, which showed that registered refugees increased from 125,493 in December 2025 to 133,400 as at Sept 30.
He said the increase of 7,907 occurred despite the Cabinet's July 23 directive for UNHCR to temporarily stop registering new refugees.
Citing the Auditor-General's Report 2/2026, Radzi said unpaid medical bills in 2025 totalled RM336 million, of which RM281 million was owed by non-citizens.
He questioned the effectiveness of the Health Ministry's "collect before discharge" approach, saying some foreign patients were allowed to leave without settling their bills when hospitals needed beds.
Radzi said mandatory insurance could also encourage UNHCR to expedite refugee resettlement in third countries, and called for the Health, Home and Foreign ministries to discuss the proposal.
In a separate written reply yesterday, Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the ministry was studying sustainable
financing options for refugees and asylum seekers,
including mandatory health insurance.
The Cabinet's July directive to
suspend new registrations
was intended to restructure refugee management under government supervision.
Doctors Without Borders subsequently called for safeguards, warning that the move could deter undocumented refugees from
seeking healthcare.

Title: Trump, Thai PM to announce trade progress, not final deal
Article:
BANGKOK: US President Donald Trump will sign a joint statement with Thailand's premier on Tuesday marking "significant progress" in trade negotiations, but will not ink a final deal, a Thai official said.
A framework agreement was unveiled just over a year ago, on the same day as Trump announced a short-lived ceasefire between Thailand and its neighbour Cambodia following deadly border clashes.
The United States is Thailand's largest export market, with the Southeast Asian nation recording a surplus of US$71.7 billion last year, according to US data.
In July, Washington imposed new tariffs of 12.5 per cent on imports from Thailand, among dozens of countries targeted in an investigation into forced labour concerns.
Thailand was also included this week among countries subject to new US export licences on advanced AI chips, intended to prevent Chinese firms from obtaining access to the technology.
Trump and Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul will make the joint statement on Tuesday at a summit of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) in the Philippines, a Thai government official said.
Deputy spokeswoman Lalida Persvivatana told AFP it marked "significant progress" in negotiations on an agreement on reciprocal trade (ART).
"However, the signing is not yet the formal ART agreement," she said, noting Thailand still needed to conduct a public consultation and legal procedures.
The US had announced trade agreements with both Thailand and Cambodia at an Asean summit in October 2025, the same day as Trump co-signed a ceasefire agreement.
The timing prompted speculation Trump had used US economic ties as leverage to try to end the conflict – one of several he says he has solved.
Long-running tensions over the border broke out into violence in July 2025, killing dozens of people.
Trump's truce proved short-lived as fighting erupted again in December, although a ceasefire agreed since then has broadly held.
The 2025 framework trade agreement envisaged a 19-per cent baseline US tariff on Thai imports and the elimination of tariffs on nearly all US goods heading into Thailand.
The two sides also agreed a non-binding memorandum outlining increased cooperation on trading rare earth minerals, which are vital to tech products and of which China is the world's leading producer.
Trump has unleashed a barrage of tariffs on trading partners since last year.
Although the Supreme Court struck down country-specific tariffs in February, Washington has since alleged insufficient action against forced labour to slap new tariffs on 60 economies, including Thailand.
Separate duties targeting sectors like steel, autos and timber remain intact.--AFP

Title: SC unveils Sukuk Prisma for climate adaption and resilience
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Securities Commission Malaysia (SC) today introduced Sukuk Prisma to the global market, a new purpose-driven sustainable sukuk framework designed to mobilise capital for climate adaptation and resilience, supporting wider sustainable development priorities.
In a statement, the SC said the framework expands the capital market's scope beyond conventional green and social categories to encompass broader climate adaptation, resilience and transitional financing, including flood mitigation, coastal protection, agriculture and the resilience of power grids.
"It also supports sukuk issuances denominated in ringgit and major hard currencies, enabling access to international capital and connecting global investors with high-impact sustainable investment opportunities," it said.
Minister of Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup launched the Sukuk Prisma at the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Türkiye.
Meanwhile, SC chairman Datuk Mohammad Faiz Azmi said: "The framework introduces a broader and clearer thematic classification to support national sustainability agenda, making it more investable, enhances investor understanding and strengthens Malaysia's position as a leader in sustainable and Islamic finance."
The SC will issue the Sukuk Prisma Framework in the first quarter of 2027. Ahead of its issuance, the SC will undertake engagements with issuers, investors and other market participants to support market readiness and encourage early adoption.

Title: 25 foreign women detained in Changkat prostitution crackdown
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Immigration officers detained 25 foreign women, including 14 from African countries, during a crackdown on suspected prostitution activities targeting tourists and foreign workers in Changkat, Bukit Bintang, early today.
The women were believed to have been soliciting customers along the popular entertainment strip, offering sexual services for about RM200.
Kuala Lumpur Immigration director Datuk Hamsha Injau said the operation, codenamed Ops Gegar, was the third conducted at the same location this year to curb prostitution and other illegal activities involving foreigners.
He said preliminary investigations found that the women had entered Malaysia individually using social visit passes before allegedly abusing the facility to engage in prostitution on a part-time basis.
"Initial investigations found that these women operated independently. They entered the country individually using social visit passes and, upon arriving in Kuala Lumpur, began looking for customers around Bukit Bintang.
"Once they secured customers, they would rent rooms at nearby hotels to carry out their activities," he said in a Facebook post today.
Hamsha said the operation was mounted following public complaints about activities that had caused discomfort among residents and visitors.
"Acting on the complaints received, I instructed our enforcement team to conduct an immediate operation.
"Our enforcement activities are carried out continuously, whether through smaller operations targeting business premises or large-scale integrated operations," he said.
The operation, which began at 1.20am, involved 35 Immigration officers of various ranks, assisted by 16 personnel from the department's Special Tactical Team (Pastak).
Hamsha said all 25 women inspected were detained for various immigration offences.
They comprised 14 women from African countries, six Myanmar nationals and five Cambodians.
The suspected offences included misuse of social visit passes, violating pass conditions and overstaying.
All detainees were taken to the Kuala Lumpur Immigration Depot for investigation under the Immigration Act 1959/63 and Immigration Regulations 1963.
Hamsha said enforcement action would continue against foreigners who violated immigration laws, as well as premises owners and employers found harbouring or employing undocumented migrants.
He also urged the public to report suspected immigration violations through the department's official channels.

Title: Malaysia approves RM812.68mil in digital investments from France between 2024 and 2026
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia approved RM812.68 million in digital investments from France between 2024 and 2026, making the country the fifth-largest European source of such investments over the period.
Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo said Malaysia wants to build on those investments by encouraging French companies to develop and commercialise new technologies with Malaysian businesses, universities and research institutions, and use the country as a base to serve the wider Asean market.
"In artificial intelligence, we welcome partnerships in research, model development, industrial applications and AI solutions for businesses and government," he said at the France-Malaysia Business Forum 2026 here today.
Also present were French President Emmanuel Macron and Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani.
Macron, who arrived in Malaysia yesterday for a two-day official visit, was accorded an official welcoming ceremony at the Sultan Abdul Samad Building in Kuala Lumpur, followed by a bilateral meeting with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
Gobind said Malaysia also sees scope for cooperation in trusted cloud infrastructure and cybersecurity, as well as chip design, research and development, and emerging technologies such as quantum computing.
He said Malaysia wants its companies to develop their own artificial intelligence (AI) solutions, create intellectual property and compete in regional and global markets. Under the 13th Malaysia Plan, the country aims for the digital economy to contribute 30 per cent of gross domestic product by 2030.
Meanwhile, the Malaysia Digital Economy Corporation (MDEC), in a statement issued in conjunction with French President Emmanuel Macron's official visit, said the approved investments involved several French companies and were projected to generate hundreds of opportunities for knowledge workers.
Among the French companies with Malaysia Digital status are AXA Group Operations Malaysia, CACEIS Malaysia of the Crédit Agricole Group, Sanofi-Aventis (Malaysia), Orange Business Services Malaysia, Schneider Electric IT Malaysia and CMA CGM Group.
MDEC said several companies were exploring opportunities to expand their presence in Malaysia, including using the country as an Asia-Pacific technology and delivery hub, with planned expansion in agentic AI, cybersecurity and automation. The agency held a networking session with French businesses and technology companies today to discuss investment opportunities and how they could use Malaysia as a base to expand into Asean.
MDEC acting chief executive officer Azlan Sharom said Malaysia offers French companies a compelling proposition to establish and scale their regional operations, supported by its digital infrastructure, investment facilitation and access to the Asean market.
"Malaysia offers French technology companies the opportunity to establish a market presence while leveraging the country as a regional base to develop technology capabilities, deliver services and expand into Asean. Through the Malaysia Digital approach, MDEC is committed to supporting companies throughout their investment journey by connecting them with the right local partners, businesses and talent, while fostering long-term partnerships that drive meaningful investments, strengthen local capabilities and promote sustainable business growth," he said.
MDEC said it would continue working with Business France, CCI France Malaysia and La French Tech Malaysia to facilitate investment and greater participation by French technology companies in Malaysia's digital economy.

Title: Trump takes reported Iran dirty bomb threat to Washington 'very seriously'
Article:
MANILA: President Donald Trump said Tuesday that US authorities take "very seriously" any possible threat to Washington, following reports Iran was planning to target officials, possibly with a radioactive bomb.
Asked about the potential threat during a visit to the Philippines, Trump said: "If there is (such a threat), they will pay a price the likes of which no other country has ever paid before."
"I hope it's not, but we take it very seriously because they happen to be crazy."
CNN, citing seven anonymous US officials, reported that US intelligence indicated that Iran was preparing to target senior Trump administration officials by detonating a so-called dirty bomb in Washington.
The report said the sources characterised Iran's plans as "an effort to give itself options rather than an indicator of an imminent attack."
A dirty bomb is a conventional explosive laced with chemical or radioactive materials.
Iran's foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei dismissed the report as "fabricated", suggesting Washington was "seeking to lay the media groundwork for their sinister designs."
"Step by step, they are attempting to manufacture a veneer of legitimacy for further aggression and atrocities," Baqaei wrote on X.
Negotiations between the United States and Iran to end their war have stalled, and Iran recently targeted US infrastructure in the Middle East.
Mediator Qatar called for restraint on Tuesday "to avoid any escalation that could undermine negotiation efforts."--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Citaglobal completes acquisition of 70pct stake in Perak hydropower assets
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Citaglobal Bhd's subsidiary, Citaglobal Renewable Energy Sdn Bhd, has completed the acquisition of 70 per cent equity interests in Zeqna Corporation Sdn Bhd and Koridor Mentari Sdn Bhd, giving the group controlling stakes in two hydropower assets in Perak.
Zeqna owns the Slim hydropower plant, while Koridor Mentari holds the Kampar hydropower project.
In a statement today, Citaglobal, which has interests in the energy, environment and connectivity sectors, said the two assets have a combined approved capacity of 12.6 megawatts (MW), with 6 MW currently operational at Slim.
Citaglobal executive chairman and president Tan Sri Mohamad Norza Zakaria said power generation is expected to become an increasingly important part of the group's energy business, with the acquisitions marking a measured step towards that goal.
"Slim and Kampar combine a plant already selling electricity to Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) with a project that has its feed-in approval and renewable energy power purchase agreement (REPPA) in place. Running one while developing the other lets us add capacity in stages, with operating experience informing each step.
"Alongside our construction and infrastructure businesses and our other energy investments, they move the group closer to the long-term recurring income we are building," he added.
Citaglobal New Energy signed a memorandum of understanding with TNB Power Generation Sdn Bhd and TIZA AI Sdn Bhd on Nov 16, 2026, to study the feasibility of supplying dedicated off-grid power to the proposed Gebeng AI Data Centre Park and discuss potential commercial arrangements.
With the Slim hydropower plant already generating recurring revenue, the group's new energy business is building a sustainable income stream while advancing its pipeline of larger-scale energy projects, Citaglobal said.

Title: Malaysian OGSE firms generate RM114.82mil in export sales as at Sept 30
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: A total of 77 Malaysian Oil and Gas Services and Equipment (OGSE) companies have generated RM114.82 million in export sales as at Sept 30 this year, said Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir.
He said the export sales were an achievement, through export promotion and international business development programmes facilitated by the Malaysia External Trade Development Corporation, reflecting progress under the National OGSE Industry Blueprint 2021-2030.
"Through the OGSE Finance Centre of Excellence, 27 companies secured RM125 million in financing approvals, while six projects under the OGSE Catalyst Programme have been commercialised, generating RM10.1 million in sales.
"These achievements reflect the importance of building commercially viable capabilities that enable Malaysian companies to compete internationally," said Akmal Nasrullah in a statement today.
He emphasised that the success of the country's internationalisation efforts should be measured by the contracts and long-term business partnerships generated and not by the number of trade missions or agreements signed.
"I have directed Malaysia Petroleum Resources Corporation (MPRC) to monitor the commercial outcomes of the Turkmenistan mission and explore similar approaches in other strategic markets," said Akmal Nasrullah.
The minister was referring to MPRC's recent Private OGSE Turkmenistan initiative under the International Market Access Programme, which brought together 40 representatives from 19 Malaysian OGSE companies at the Oil & Gas Turkmenistan (OGT) 2026 Conference and Exhibition last month.
The mission saw MPRC sign a memorandum of understanding with State Concern Turkmennebit, Turkmenistan's national oil company, to explore mutually beneficial business opportunities.
MPRC also organised its first country pavilion at OGT, showcasing the expertise and technological capabilities of seven Malaysian OGSE companies.
Akmal Nasrullah said MPRC had also facilitated strategic engagements and business matching involving government representatives, national energy companies and international operators, building on more than 30 years of Malaysia-Turkmenistan oil and gas relations led by Petronas.
These included Dragon Oil (Turkmenistan) Ltd, Eni Turkmenistan Limited and China National Petroleum Corporation (CNPC) Turkmenistan.
He said the industry was also diversifying into low-carbon energy value chains, with four OGSE companies securing RM18.5 million in energy transition-related financing.
"To ensure the National OGSE Industry Blueprint reflects the needs and potential of the industry nationwide, I have invited stakeholders from Sabah and Sarawak to present their developments and priorities at the next steering committee meeting," said Akmal Nasrullah.
MPRC president and chief executive officer Mohd Yazid Ja'afar said the OGSE Strategic Partnership Support Programme has facilitated 37 companies through business matching and strategic collaborations.
"The blueprint provides a framework for coordinated action across government and industry. Continued collaboration among implementation partners is essential to address industry needs and sustain the momentum of these initiatives," he said.
The OGSE Blueprint Implementation Steering Committee meeting also reviewed the blueprint's implementation progress, with representatives from various ministries and industry stakeholders attending.
Marking five years of implementation, the annual National OGSE Blueprint Forum will be held in Kuala Lumpur on Dec 3, with Akmal Nasrullah scheduled to officiate the event and participate in a panel discussion moderated by Mohd Yazid.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar orders immediate aid for family of policeman killed in Sungkai crash
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has directed immediate assistance to be provided to the family of a policeman killed in an accident involving a police van in Sungkai, Perak, today, as well as to other officers injured in the incident.
In a Facebook post, Anwar said he had instructed his political secretary, Kamil Munim, to deliver contributions to the family of the late Muhammad Shahrul Aliff Yaacob and the injured officers.
He also conveyed his condolences to the deceased's family, praying that they would be granted strength and fortitude in facing their loss, while wishing the injured officers a speedy recovery.
"My condolences to the family of the late Muhammad Shahrul Aliff Yaacob, a police officer who lost his life in an accident involving a police van in Sungkai, Perak, today.
"May his family be granted strength and fortitude in facing this loss, and may the injured police officers have a speedy recovery. Al-Fatihah," he said.
In the incident
, one policeman was killed and 10 others injured after the PDRM van they were travelling in skidded and crashed into a metal guardrail at KM352 of the North-South Expressway (southbound), near Tapah, today.
