Title: Malaysian palm oil industry well-positioned for EUDR compliance – MPOB
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's oil palm industry is well-positioned to meet the requirements of the European Union Deforestation Regulation (EUDR), backed by a longstanding sustainability framework, mandatory national certification and ongoing efforts to strengthen digital traceability across the supply chain.
The Malaysian Palm Oil Board (MPOB) in a statement said Malaysia is moving beyond sustainability commitments towards a system that could demonstrate, through verifiable information, where its palm oil comes from, how it is produced and how it moves through the supply chain.
"As the EUDR implementation deadline approaches, Malaysia's priority is to ensure that its established sustainability framework is translated into reliable, accessible and verifiable information that supports operators and exporters in meeting their respective due diligence obligations," it said.
The MPOB noted that the Malaysian Sustainable Palm Oil (MSPO) certification scheme was introduced in 2013, with implementation commencing in 2015, reflecting the country's recognition that responsible production and environmental stewardship are fundamental to the industry's long-term competitiveness.
The MSPO 2.0 standard, under MS 2530:2022, provides assurance through independent third-party certification covering legal compliance, environmental protection, traceability, social safeguards and responsible production practices, it said.
Currently, 92.36 per cent of Malaysia's 5.7 million hectares of oil palm planted area has been MSPO-certified, including approximately 181,000 independent smallholders, reflecting the country's commitment to making sustainability a shared responsibility across the industry.
"While MSPO certification does not automatically establish EUDR compliance, it provides important supporting evidence for operators undertaking their due diligence, particularly in demonstrating legal production, responsible land management and sustainability practices," it said.
It added that Malaysia is strengthening digital traceability in the oil palm industry through the development and enhancement of three complementary digital systems, namely GeoSAWIT, e-MSPO, and the Sawit Intelligent Management System (SIMS).
"Moving forward, these three systems will be progressively integrated to establish a more connected digital traceability framework for the Malaysian oil palm industry.
"This integration is intended to link geospatial information, certification records and commercial transaction data, providing a more comprehensive picture of the supply chain, from oil palm production areas and smallholder plots to dealers, mills and other industry operators," it said.
Besides, Malaysia's efforts to align its sustainability framework with international requirements have also received encouraging recognition, such as the Netherlands Food and Consumer Product Safety Authority.
Meanwhile, MPOB director general Datuk Badrul Hisham Mohd said Malaysia's approach to sustainability goes beyond meeting regulatory requirements.
"We are committed to demonstrating, through credible certification, reliable data and transparent supply chains, that Malaysian palm oil is produced responsibly.
"Equally important, we want to ensure that every segment of the industry, including independent smallholders, can continue to participate in and benefit from international markets," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Police seek dashcam footage of fatal Penang crash
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Police are seeking dashcam footage and eyewitnesses to assist investigations into a
collision
that killed a mother and left her 6-year-old daughter critically injured in Tanjung Bungah today.
Northeast district police chief Assistant Commissioner Abdul Rozak Muhammad said investigators were piecing together the circumstances surrounding the 1pm accident along Jalan Lembah Permai.
He said initial investigations found that the 36-year-old motorcyclist was heading home to Batu Ferringhi from Penang Hospital with her daughter when she lost control of her motorcycle.
"She subsequently veered into the opposite lane and collided head-on with an oncoming sport utility vehicle (SUV) driven by a 33-year-old woman," he said in a statement.
Abdul Rozak said the motorcyclist was pronounced dead at the scene, while her daughter sustained chest injuries and was taken back to Penang Hospital for treatment.
The SUV driver escaped unhurt.
He said police were alerted to the accident by members of the public at 1.20pm.
The case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987 for causing death by reckless or dangerous driving.
Those with information are urged to contact investigating officer Inspector Mohd Shahid Othman at 017-267 0543.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Tuanku Muhriz grants Ismail audience amid Negri Sembilan constitutional crisis
Article:
SEREMBAN: The Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, granted an audience today to Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim following the current political impasse affecting the state.
It is understood that the audience took place between 5pm and 6.30pm; however, details regarding the meeting remain unconfirmed.
Yesterday, it was reported that Ismail, 67, who is Juasseh state assemblyman,
had resigned
from his position as menteri besar.
Earlier this morning, the Negri Sembilan Palace said the menteri besar's resignation
would only take effect
upon receiving the consent of Tuanku Muhriz, in accordance with the provisions of the Negri Sembilan state constitution.
Comptroller of the Royal Household Datuk Azizi Mohamad Ali said the Negri Sembilan Palace had taken note of a statement by Barisan Nasional (BN) secretary-general Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir posted on social media at 10pm last night regarding Ismail's resignation.
Yesterday, Zambry said BN chairman and Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi had received a copy of the resignation letter, which had been addressed to Tuanku Muhriz.
Ismail was sworn in as Negri Sembilan menteri besar on Aug 2.
In the 16th Negri Sembilan state election, BN secured 18 state assembly seats, while Perikatan Nasional (PN) won seven, enabling the two coalitions to form the state government with a two-thirds majority. - BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: GTA Holdings, France's Safran team up on helicopter engine maintenance
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: GTA Holdings Bhd has teamed up with France's Safran Group to develop helicopter engine repair and training capabilities in Malaysia.
This follows a non-binding memorandum of understanding (MoU) signed by their respective subsidiaries, Global Turbine Asia Sdn Bhd and Safran Helicopter Engines Asia Pte Ltd.
GTA said the proposed cooperation could help it secure higher-value maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO) opportunities, including potential demand from the Royal Malaysian Air Force's (RMAF) proposed acquisition of four additional Airbus helicopters.
"Under the proposed cooperation, the parties will explore the development of Makila 2 LRU Level 4 maintenance and operational capabilities through the potential transfer of knowledge, specialised technical training and qualification of Malaysian personnel.
"Safran Helicopter will explore the provision of OEM repair know-how, procedures, technical data and training support, while Global Turbine will evaluate the necessary investment in facilities, tooling, test benches, equipment and qualified personnel," it said in a statement.
GTA said both parties plan to establish a joint working group to assess the project's technical requirements, implementation timeline, resources and responsibilities.
Global Turbine currently provides maintenance support for the Makila 2A1 engines used in the RMAF's existing H225M helicopter fleet and has been a Safran-certified maintenance centre in Malaysia for more than 15 years.
GTA said the proposed fleet expansion could generate additional MRO opportunities over the lifespan of the new engines.
Any potential contribution would depend on the government's procurement decision, the scope of maintenance work, contractual arrangements and relevant approvals.
GTA managing director and chief executive officer Datuk Nonee Ashirin Mohd Radzi said the collaboration supported the company's efforts to strengthen local technical expertise and expand its presence in the regional aerospace MRO market.
"Through our cooperation with Safran Helicopter, we aim to explore new opportunities to strengthen local technical capabilities, develop Malaysian aerospace talent and expand our participation in the regional MRO value chain.
"For GTA Holdings, this represents more than a potential expansion of services. It is an opportunity to build a stronger, higher-value aerospace business, supported by technical excellence, disciplined investment and long-term commercial partnerships," she said.
GTA said the MoU was formalised in conjunction with French President Emmanuel Macron's official visit to Malaysia on Nov 16 and 17, reflecting broader industrial cooperation between the two countries.
Both parties also intend to propose the collaboration for consideration under the industrial collaboration programme associated with the RMAF's proposed helicopter acquisition.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Autistic girl, 6, fighting for life after Penang crash kills mother
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: A 6-year-old autistic girl is fighting for her life after her mother was killed in a
road accident
while returning from a routine hospital visit today.
The pair had just left Penang Hospital after the child's monthly specialist check-up and were riding their motorcycle towards Batu Ferringhi when the collision occurred.
The crash happened along a stretch near the school attended by the girl, Seroja Dania, initially leading to assumptions that they had just left the premises.
However, the girl had skipped classes today to attend her medical appointment.
The deceased's younger brother, Muhammad Firdaus Muhammad Lizan, 32, said his sister, Amira Mohd Lizan, 36, had earlier finished selling nasi lemak and kuih with their mother before taking her youngest daughter to the hospital.
"She was not returning from school as initially thought; the crash just happened near her daughter's school. They had actually just returned from the hospital," he said when met at the Penang Hospital mortuary.
"Every month, she brings Seroja Dania, who is an OKU cardholder, for her specialist check-up at the hospital," he added.
Firdaus said Seroja Dania remained in critical condition at the hospital's emergency unit, dispelling earlier rumours in their village that both mother and daughter had died.
"At first, the village was informed there were two deaths and preparations were made to dig two graves, before we clarified that the child is still alive, though very critical," he said.
He described his sister as a kind and helpful person who had shown no unusual behaviour when they last met two days ago.
Amira leaves behind three daughters, including Seroja Dania and two older girls, aged 12 and 13, who are staying at a boarding school.
Firdaus said he rushed to the mortuary with their mother after receiving news of the tragedy, adding that the family had yet to receive full details on the cause of the collision.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Health Ministry has only 19 cardiothoracic surgeons
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Only 19 cardiothoracic surgeons are currently serving at six of the seven Health Ministry hospitals offering heart surgery.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said 37 medical officers were undergoing specialist training, comprising four under Universiti Teknologi Mara's Master of Surgery programme and 33 through the parallel pathway.
He was responding to Dr Ahmad Yunus Hairi (PN-Kuala Langat), who proposed easing entry requirements for cardiothoracic specialist training to address the nationwide shortage.
Yunus cited the resignation of the ministry's head of cardiothoracic surgery services, Dr Basheer Ahamed Abdul Kareem, on Oct 23.
He also referred to the ministry's target of producing 800 medical specialists and 700 dental specialists annually, supported by an allocation of RM165 million, as well as RM239 million for specialist training scholarships for medical and dental officers.
"How many cardiothoracic specialists do we plan to train, and how many scholarships can be provided for this expertise?
"The government should ease the admission of medical officers for cardiothoracic specialisation training," he said while debating the ministry's allocation at the committee stage.
Winding up the committee-stage debate on the Health Ministry's allocation under the Supply Bill 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat today, Dzulkefly said cardiothoracic surgery was a highly specialised service requiring support from anaesthetists, cardiologists, perfusionists and trained personnel, including operating theatre nurses.
He said the service was provided regionally, with specialists travelling to hospitals without resident cardiothoracic surgeons to perform operations.
The ministry's current strategy was to strengthen its seven existing cardiothoracic centres, prioritising hospitals with no resident specialist or only one, including Hospital Raja Perempuan Zainab II and Hospital Queen Elizabeth II.
In the short term, the ministry was using its Hospital Services Outsourcing Programme for cardiology and cardiothoracic services to meet demand for heart surgery.
Dzulkefly said amendments to the Medical Act 1971 had also resolved registration issues faced by specialists returning from overseas training, including those under parallel pathway programmes.
The Medical (Amendment) Act 2024, gazetted in October 2024, allows
specialists trained
under the ministry's parallel pathway programme to apply for inclusion in the National Specialist Register through the Malaysian Medical Council.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Shah Alam Line resumes normal operations after tree falls on tracks [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Rapid KL's Shah Alam Line has resumed normal operations after a fallen tree disrupted train services near UiTM Shah Alam station earlier today.
In a statement, Rapid KL said the tree fell onto the tracks following bad weather at 5.22pm, forcing services to be suspended for more than an hour.
Normal operations resumed at 6.43pm.
Passengers were safely evacuated at Dato Menteri station, with no injuries reported.
A technical team was deployed to remove the fallen tree and debris from the tracks to allow services to resume safely.
The operator said its operations team would continue monitoring train services to ensure they remained safe and stable.
Passengers were advised to check Rapid KL's official social media channels or the MyRapid PULSE app for service updates.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Bangladeshi worker killed in Kepong landslide
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A 34-year-old Bangladeshi worker was killed after being buried under tonnes of earth in a landslide at Kampung Melayu Kepong here today.
The victim was found at 5.14pm following a search and rescue operation involving firefighters and other agencies.
Kuala Lumpur Fire and Rescue Department operations commander Mohd Hafizan Hassan said the department received an emergency call at 2.45pm.
He said eight firefighters from the Jinjang Fire and Rescue Station were dispatched to the scene at No. 4, Jalan 2A/1, Kampung Melayu Kepong.
"The team arrived at 2.55pm and confirmed that a landslide had occurred at the location.
"Initial investigations revealed that a worker in the area had been buried beneath the collapsed earth," he said in a statement today.
Hafizan said firefighters immediately began excavation works to locate the victim.
An excavator was deployed to assist in removing the earth, with the operation carried out in cooperation with other agencies.
"The victim, a 34-year-old Bangladeshi man, was found at 5.14pm and handed over to police for further action," he said.
The worker was later confirmed dead.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Flash floods close Bukit Raja interchange, disrupt traffic on major highways
Article:
SHAH ALAM: Flash floods following heavy rain this afternoon forced the closure of the Bukit Raja interchange and caused traffic congestion along several major highways in Selangor.
Plus Malaysia Berhad, in an update on X at 5.53pm, announced that the southbound Bukit Raja interchange on the New Klang Valley Expressway (NKVE), heading towards Section 7, Shah Alam, had been closed due to flooding.
The highway operator said floodwaters had inundated the area outside its maintenance facility near Section 7 and i-City, resulting in heavy traffic congestion.
"Heavy traffic. Drive carefully," it said.
Meanwhile, the Malaysian Highway Authority (MHA) reported flash floods at several locations along the Shah Alam Expressway (Kesas).
In an update at 3.31pm, MHA said floodwaters had affected KM27.3 of the highway, westbound from the Kemuning Toll Plaza, causing traffic congestion.
However, no lanes were reported blocked at the time.
Photographs shared by MHA showed a section of the highway covered in muddy floodwaters, with traffic cones placed along the affected stretch. Several heavy vehicles were also seen travelling along the road.
In a separate update at 3.42pm, MHA reported that flash floods had affected the motorcycle lane at KM28.0 of KESAS, eastbound from Kemuning towards Bukit Rimau.
It said the motorcycle lane was obstructed by floodwaters, although traffic remained under control.
A photograph accompanying the update showed floodwaters covering the motorcycle lane and part of the surrounding road, while vehicles continued moving along the adjacent carriageway.
In another update at 4.04pm, MHA reported water overflowing onto the road at the West Coast Expressway (WCE) interchange connecting Jalan Meru to the Bandar Bukit Raja Selatan junction.
It said no lanes were obstructed and traffic remained under control at the time.
Motorists were advised to remain vigilant and exercise caution while travelling along the affected routes.
The incidents came amid reports of flash floods in several parts of Selangor this afternoon, including Shah Alam, Klang, Puncak Alam and Ijok.
Motorists travelling through flood-prone areas are advised to use alternative routes where possible and avoid driving or riding through submerged roads.
Floodwaters can conceal potholes, open drains and damaged road surfaces, while strong currents may cause vehicles to lose traction or become stranded.
Motorcyclists face additional risks, as even relatively shallow floodwaters can cause them to lose balance.
Drivers are also advised to check traffic updates from highway operators and authorities before beginning their journeys.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: SkyeChip, France's SiPearl team up on next-generation computing platform
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: SkyeChip Bhd has signed a non-binding memorandum of understanding (MoU) with France-based SiPearl SAS to jointly develop and commercialise a next-generation computing platform based on Arm Neoverse Compute Subsystems (CSS).
The collaboration will be undertaken through a joint venture (JV) company to be incorporated in Malaysia by December, with SkyeChip expected to hold a 51 per cent stake and SiPearl the remaining 49 per cent.
The JV would combine SiPearl's expertise in system-level architecture and server central processing units (CPUs) with SkyeChip's silicon intellectual property (IP) portfolio, including high-bandwidth memory interfaces, Network-on-Chip and die-to-die interface IP.
The partnership aims to develop a differentiated processor and system solution while accelerating development, reducing costs and expanding market access.
SkyeChip said the proposed JV would apply to the relevant Malaysian authorities for an Arm Neoverse CSS licence.
Subject to approval, both companies will jointly define the platform specifications before proceeding with silicon development, tape-out and post-silicon activities through the JV, with the aim of moving towards production and commercialisation.
SkyeChip chief executive officer and founder Datuk Fong Swee Kiang said the partnership would strengthen the company's capabilities in advanced semiconductor design and high-performance computing.
"Through this partnership, we aim to accelerate development, optimise costs and widen our market reach across Asia, North America and Europe.
"We believe this collaboration will contribute to the growing semiconductor ecosystems in Malaysia and Europe, particularly in advanced IC design and high-performance computing," he said in a statement.
SiPearl chief executive officer and founder Philippe Notton said the collaboration would leverage the company's expertise in Arm-based processor technology following the development of its first-generation CPU, Rhea1, for supercomputing and artificial intelligence.
The establishment of the JV remains subject to definitive agreements, which both parties aim to negotiate within 90 days of the MoU.
The collaboration is also subject to board approvals, relevant regulatory and export control clearances, and the granting of the Arm Neoverse CSS licence.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Trump in Manila for Asean-US talks
Article:
MANILA: US President Donald Trump arrived in the Philippines this afternoon to attend the 49th Asean Summit and Related Summits, marking his first visit to the country in nine years.
Air Force One, carrying Trump, landed at the Balagbag Ramp of Ninoy Aquino International Airport in Pasay City at 5.33pm.
He was welcomed by Executive Secretary Ralph Recto, Ilocos Norte Representative Sandro Marcos, Philippine Ambassador to the United States Jose Manuel Romualdez and US Ambassador to the Philippines Lee Lipton.
Trump subsequently attended the Asean-US Special Summit at the Philippine International Convention Centre (PICC).
He is scheduled to meet regional leaders tonight to discuss shared interests and strengthen cooperation between Washington and Asean member states.
He is also expected to hold bilateral talks with Philippine President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr on the sidelines of the summit.
The meeting is expected to provide an opportunity for both leaders to discuss longstanding ties between Manila and Washington, particularly in defence and security, trade and investment, as well as regional developments.
Trump's visit comes as the Philippines steps up cooperation with the US on economic security initiatives, including critical minerals, semiconductors and emerging technologies through the Washington-led Pax Silica initiative.
Trump last visited the Philippines in November 2017 to attend the 31st Asean Summit and Related Summits during his first term as US president.
His participation in this year's summit reflects Washington's continued commitment to strengthening ties with Asean, amid an increasingly dynamic geopolitical and economic landscape in the Indo-Pacific region.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Dialog Group posts higher net profit of RM165mil in Q1
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Dialog Group Bhd posted a higher net profit of RM165.07 million in the first quarter ended Sept 30, 2026 (Q1 FY27) compared to RM140.01 million in the same period last year.
It said in a Bursa Malaysia filing today that revenue rose to RM787.04 million in Q1 FY27 compared to RM656.99 million previously, driven by strong contributions across its businesses, particularly from its Malaysian operations, reflecting the resilience of its business model and continued execution excellence.
On prospects, the company said it remains focused on executing its key long-term strategies as a leading integrated technical services provider with diversified operations across the upstream, midstream and downstream businesses.
"Supported by our dedicated management team, we are confident that our business model is well structured to navigate against headwinds arising from economic uncertainty, oil price volatility and currency movements, and the ongoing geopolitical conflict in West Asia.
"Dialog remains focused on diversifying across the energy sector to navigate economic and oil price cycles, consistent with the group's strategy of generating long-term recurring income," it said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Health Ministry to get 1,389 new ambulances after failed supply deal
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Health Ministry will receive 1,389 new ambulances, following a decision not to renew an earlier supply contract after the appointed company delivered only 115 of the 590 units ordered.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said suppliers for 989 ambulances would be finalised next month, while another 400 units had been approved under the 2027 Budget.
"The ministry was supposed to receive 590 new ambulances by the end of 2024 at the latest, through a contract awarded in 2022.
"However, the appointed company was only able to supply 115 ambulances throughout the contract period, which ended in November 2024.
"This led the ministry to decide not to renew the contract. Otherwise we will be rewarding failures after failures," he said when winding up the committee-stage debate on the Health Ministry's allocation under the Supply Bill 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat.
Datuk Dr Mohd Radzi Md Jidin (PN-Putrajaya) had earlier raised the matter, asking about the status of the previous procurement and why a new allocation for 400 ambulances had been made despite the earlier order remaining unfulfilled.
He had also inquired and asked Dzulkefly who had awarded the earlier contract.
"Don't ask me which contract, who gave it, which minister gave it. That is all water under the bridge.
"I don't want to politicise health and I don't want to weaponise health. This is my principle," Dzulkefly said.
He said the ministry had since realigned its existing allocation and secured additional funding for a new ambulance contract.
The procurement of 989 ambulances was now at its final stage, he said, adding that the ministry's procurement board decision had been referred to the Finance Ministry, which had informed the Health Ministry of its decision.
Dzulkefly said the new contract would be divided among six suppliers instead of being awarded to a single company.
"We are against the idea of one winner takes all. That is the old era. We really want to have shared prosperity.
"We don't want to put all eggs in one basket," he said.
He said the appointment of the suppliers would be finalised in December, with all 989 ambulances expected to be delivered in stages.
The government had also approved funding for another 400 ambulances under the 2027 Budget, bringing the total number of new units for the ministry to 1,389.
"This number is expected to address the current shortage of ambulances," he said.
Last month, Dzulkefly told the Dewan Rakyat that only 34.1 per cent of ambulance responses to critical cases last year arrived within the 15-minute target, below the ministry's 50 per cent benchmark.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Macron departs Malaysia after two-day official visit
Article:
SEPANG: French President Emmanuel Macron departed Malaysia today after concluding his two-day official visit, made at the invitation of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
The visit was Macron's first to Malaysia since he assumed office in May 2017.
The special aircraft carrying Macron, his wife Brigitte Macron and their delegation took off from the Bunga Raya Complex at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) at 6.05pm.
Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo was present to bid farewell to Macron and his delegation.
Before his departure, Macron inspected a guard of honour mounted by 28 officers and personnel from the First Battalion of the Royal Ranger Regiment, led by Captain Luqman Hakim Abd Khar.
A cultural performance by the National Department for Culture and Arts (JKKN) troupe was also held to mark his departure, showcasing Malaysia's multicultural heritage through traditional dances and musical performances featuring traditional instruments.
Earlier today, Macron was accorded an official welcome at the Sultan Abdul Samad Building before holding bilateral talks with Anwar.
The discussions focused on elevating Malaysia-France relations to a Strategic Partnership, reflecting the growing depth and strategic significance of the longstanding ties between the two countries.
In 2025, total trade between Malaysia and France amounted to RM17.78 billion (US$4.17 billion).
Malaysia's exports to France were valued at RM6.05 billion (US$1.41 billion), with electrical and electronic products forming the principal export category.
Imports from France totalled RM11.73 billion (US$2.76 billion), comprising mainly transport equipment, machinery and chemicals.
France is Malaysia's 21st-largest trading partner globally and its fourth-largest among European countries.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Court allows partial challenge over Kluang council's stray dog SOPs
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Court of Appeal today granted leave to the Kluang Animal Protection Association to pursue a judicial review challenging the Kluang Municipal Council's (MPK) handling of stray dogs.
A three-member bench comprising Justices Datuk Dr Shahnaz Sulaiman, Datuk Amarjeet Singh and Alice Loke Yee Ching granted leave for two remedies sought by the association: a certiorari order and declaratory reliefs.
However, the court declined to grant leave for other remedies sought, namely a mandamus order, damages and a prohibitory order.
Delivering the unanimous decision, Justice Shahnaz said there was an arguable case for certiorari and declaratory relief, which ought to be ventilated at the substantive hearing.
"We allow in part this appeal. We grant leave for the relief of certiorari and declaration to proceed at the substantive stage," said Shahnaz.
Shahnaz also said the association's judicial review application, filed on May 7 last year, had been submitted within the prescribed time limit.
The panel remitted the case to the Johor Baru High Court for the substantive application to be heard by a different judge or judicial commissioner. Case management was fixed for Nov 24.
The association had filed the judicial review against MPK and its president, seeking declarations that the council had breached the Housing and Local Government Ministry secretary-general's standard operating procedures (SOPs) on capturing and disposing of stray dogs in the municipality.
MPK denied allegations of mistreatment, maintaining that the dogs were disposed of in accordance with the SOPs.
On July 21 last year, the High Court dismissed the association's application for leave to commence judicial review proceedings.
At today's proceedings, lawyers Gavin Jayapal and Parveena Kaur represented the association while Senior Federal Counsel Suhana Sabil appeared for the Attorney-General. - BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: BN demands disclosure of KLSCAH land premium assessment
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Barisan Nasional has demanded that the government disclose the formula, valuation basis and approval minutes behind the reduction of the Kuala Lumpur and Selangor Chinese Assembly Hall (KLSCAH) land premium from RM4.67 million to RM1,000.
Manndzri Nasib (BN-Tenggara) said the substantial reduction for the renewal of the 99-year lease raised questions about transparency, governance and public revenue management.
"Do not hide behind discretionary powers. The ministry must disclose the circulars, official calculation formula and valuation basis used to reduce the premium from RM4.67 million to RM1,000 following the change in land use from commercial to institutional," he said at a press conference in parliament today.
Previously, Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said the RM1,000 premium was imposed after KLSCAH agreed to reclassify the land for institutional use, giving up its potential for commercial development such as condominiums or shopping malls.
Yeoh said the 103-year-old building was gazetted as a heritage building in 2007.
Manndzri said BN recognised the Chinese community's contribution to preserving KLSCAH as a national heritage site but maintained that its heritage and institutional status should not exempt the land premium assessment from scrutiny.
He said the site's original valuation stood at RM4.67 million despite the building's heritage status.
"Such technical justifications cannot be used as a shield to deflect broader questions about governance," he said.
He also questioned the potential loss of government revenue, saying the foregone premium could have been used to upgrade People's Housing Project facilities, assist the B40 group or fund flood mitigation projects in Kuala Lumpur.
Manndzri further urged the government to guarantee that the building would not be used for profit-making commercial rental activities.
He also proposed a clause allowing the government to recover the land's market value if the stipulated land-use conditions were breached.
BN also sought clarification on whether the same nominal premium would apply to charitable organisations, places of worship and other ethnic heritage bodies in the Federal Territories under similar circumstances.
Manndzri questioned the decision to grant a 99-year lease when eight years remained on the original lease, and called for clarification on the land-use conditions and compliance monitoring mechanisms.
He said the ministry should also explain how the land was deemed to have no commercial development value following its reclassification as institutional land, and how the restrictions were factored into the RM1,000 premium assessment.
"BN will not compromise on the integrity of national assets and revenue management. The government cannot simply chant slogans about good governance but fail to practise them when faced with decisions that create perceptions of favouritism.
"The minister responsible must answer all these questions comprehensively and be prepared to explain the matter in the Dewan Rakyat.
"We demand transparent and consistent valuations for all institutions in similar circumstances," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: RM2.7bil Salam project to bolster national digital security: Fahmi
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The RM2.7 billion madani Submarine Cable Connection (Salam) project will strengthen the resilience and security of Malaysia's digital network while boosting connectivity between Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah and Sarawak.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the project, implemented by Telekom Malaysia (TM), spans about 5,500km with 10 landing stations.
"Most importantly, we are not merely increasing capacity. We are building a more resilient, secure and future-ready national digital network, one that includes Sabah and Sarawak," he said in a Facebook post today.
Fahmi said the project uses technology from France-based Alcatel Submarine Networks (ASN), a global leader in the field.
He added that Salam will provide alternative routes during submarine cable disruptions while supporting 5G networks, cloud services, artificial intelligence (AI) and data centres.
According to the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC), work on the project is scheduled to begin in mid-December 2026, with completion expected in phases by the first quarter of 2030.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia eyes French expertise for power grid
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia can deepen its strategic ties with France by attracting French investments into the country's energy supply chain, particularly in manufacturing submarine and land-based cables to support the proposed Asean Power Grid.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof said Malaysia could leverage France's expertise in energy infrastructure, including cable manufacturing and turbines, to develop local capabilities and strengthen regional connectivity.
He said discussions covered opportunities for French investors to establish cable manufacturing facilities in Malaysia.
This is necessary given the extensive infrastructure required to connect Southeast Asian countries through the Asean Power Grid.
"France has the whole value chain. It makes cables, both sea-based and land-based cables. It also makes turbines," he told reporters at a media engagement session organised by the Energy Transition and Water Transformation Ministry here today.
Fadillah said the proposed grid will require extensive undersea and land-based connections involving countries such as Vietnam, Malaysia, Indonesia, the Philippines and Sarawak.
"If we can do it here, of course, it will be more competitive," he said, adding that local manufacturing could also improve the competitiveness of installation costs.
He said Malaysia is also exploring broader cooperation with France across the energy value chain.
This includes technical training, public engagement, access to existing technologies and efforts to strengthen domestic energy capabilities.
Separately, Fadillah said the government is studying ways to maximise the use of existing water infrastructure and underutilised assets amid growing resource constraints.
This includes exploring the conversion of unused ponds into reservoirs to store and process water for use during dry periods.
He said some existing facilities were still operational while others became inactive, prompting the government to assess options to rehabilitate, repurpose or open them up to private sector participation.
The relevant department will evaluate how these assets could be optimised to serve multiple purposes, including recreation and urban development.
On water infrastructure spending, Fadillah said a project in Johor is currently under construction with an allocation of nearly RM100 million for various components.
Under the 13th Malaysia Plan, another RM600 million has been allocated for the construction of a water treatment facility in Pasir Gudang, Johor.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PEOPLElogy’s leaders conference rallies corporate Malaysia to put people first in AI push, as ex-HRD Corp chief warns against cutting training
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Nov 17 — Corporate Malaysia must keep investing in its people to get real value from artificial intelligence (AI), Green Packet Bhd managing director and group chief executive officer Datuk Shahul Hameed Shaik Dawood said as PEOPLElogy Berhad opened its Build a Future Team (BAFT) Leaders Conference 2026 today.
In a media release, the former HRD Corp chief executive warned companies against cutting training when business gets tough.
“The question should no longer be, ‘Can I afford to train my people?’ But rather, ‘Can I afford not to?’ Technology can be bought. Capability has to be built,” he said.
PEOPLElogy founder and managing director Allen Lee said: “Datuk Shahul has said what every leader in this room needs to hear. AI will only be as good as the people we prepare to use it, and that preparation cannot wait for better times. BAFT is where corporate Malaysia commits to that work.”
Allen said leaders would be invited tomorrow to make a Leaders Declaration, pledging to keep people at the heart of their AI decisions and to help every team member take their first step so that no one is left behind.
Welcoming delegates, PEOPLElogy Head of corporate planning Serene Tan, who heads the organising committee, said last week’s I’m AI READY Summit showed that readiness was about attitude, not technical skill.
“Being AI ready is not about being technical. It is about being willing. Willing to learn, willing to ask, and willing to admit what we do not yet know,” she added in the media release.
“AI can make our organisations faster, but only people can decide what that speed is for.”
AI will only be as good as the people we prepare to use it, and that preparation cannot wait for better times, said PEOPLElogy Berhad founder and managing director Allen Lee. — Picture by PEOPLElogy Berhad
Now in its fourth year, the two-day conference at Marriott Petaling Jaya brings corporate leaders and government together to plan their future teams around AI, under the theme HumAnIze: Leading with Purpose in an AI Economy. Its sessions follow six pillars, Discover, Design, Develop, Digitalize, Deploy and Declare, taking leaders from assessing where their organisations stand to declaring their AI readiness.
Today’s programme included the Leaders’ AI Competency Lab, an interactive workshop where leaders worked towards a 90-day capability plan.
BAFT follows the three-day I’m AI READY Summit at The Campus Ampang, opened by Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo on Nov 12, where SMEs, students and workers took AI-readiness assessments and received personalised upskilling roadmaps.
Speakers there urged Malaysians to use AI without losing the critical thinking employers value most.
Former deputy international trade and industry minister Prof Dr Ong Kian Ming, an adjunct professor at Taylor’s University, said he had taken on more than 200 interns over the past decade, and those who stood out were proactive and added value.
He urged students to build a LinkedIn portfolio early but keep it personal. “It cannot be 100 per cent AI-generated. Having AI-generated components is not necessarily bad, but you must use it creatively,” he said.
Pos Malaysia’s Natalia Navin said employers must be honest about AI’s impact on jobs. “I won’t say to any employee that AI won’t take your job. AI can take over some tasks. Employers must just be honest, and that is how you build trust,” she said.
Both events are part of National AI Readiness Week 2026 (NAIRW 2026), the flagship of PEOPLElogy’s I’m AI READY movement, which aims to get 5 million Malaysians to declare their AI readiness by 2030, in collaboration with MyDIGITAL Corporation.
The week closes tomorrow with the Asia AI Excellence Awards 2026 Gala Dinner, recognising organisations setting the benchmark for responsible AI adoption.

Title: Firemen rescue 16 people aged 65 to 85, after flash floods hit Kluang nursing home
Article:
KLUANG, Nov 17 — Firemen rescued 16 elderly residents from a nursing home hit by flash floods following a downpour in Jalan Haji Manan here today.
In a press statement, Kluang Fire and Rescue Station operations commander Fadly A. Karim said the station received an emergency call at 5.11pm.
He said 12 firemen, supported by a Fire Rescue Tender (FRT) vehicle and a four-wheel-drive, were immediately dispatched to the scene about a kilometre away.
“Upon arrival, the operations team discovered that a flash flood had caused water levels in the areas surrounding the nursing home to rise to more than 0.6 metres (about two feet) after the heavy rain.
“The team carried out a rescue operation where 16 elderly residents, comprising 14 men and two women, were evacuated to a safer area,” he said.
Firefighters help evacuate 16 people from a flooded nursing home on Jalan Haji Manan in Kluang, November 17, 2026. — Picture courtesy of the Johor Fire and Rescue Department
Fadly said the residents, aged between 65 and 85, were later relocated to a homestay in Jalan 17, Yap Tau Sah.
He said firemen also monitored the flood situation in the surrounding areas before concluding the operation at 5.31pm.

Title: Policeman whose wrist was severed in Kepong machete attack considered for field promotion
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 17 — A policeman whose right wrist was severed in a machete attack by a foreign man in Desa Aman Puri, Kepong, on November 11 is being considered for a field promotion.
Bukit Aman Crime Prevention and Community Safety Department (JPJKK) director Datuk Noor Hisam Nordin said Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail had proposed the promotion in recognition of the officer’s dedication to duty.
“We are processing the necessary documentation through the Selangor Police Contingent.
“We are also looking into other entitlements, including a possible medal award and assistance from several welfare funds,” he told reporters after visiting the officer at Kuala Lumpur Hospital (HKL) today.
Also present were Deputy Inspector-General of Police Datuk Seri Abdul Aziz Abdul Majid, Bukit Aman JPJKK Deputy Directors Datuk Suryani Sungit and Datuk Nik Ros Azhan Nik Ab Hamid, and Selangor JPJKK chief Senior Assistant Commissioner Mohamad Fakhrudin Abdul Hamid.
On the officer’s condition, Noor Hisam said the 26-year-old Lance Corporal was showing positive progress and was now stable, although he remained in critical condition.
He said doctors had indicated that another three to four weeks would be needed for the injured nerves and bones to recover during this critical phase.
“He is in a general ward but remains under close observation. He is conscious, able to communicate and showing strong determination.
“When I spoke to him earlier, he said he had begun to regain sensation in his fingers, although he had not fully recovered and still needed treatment,” he said.
Noor Hisam said the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) was also providing welfare assistance to the officer’s family by bringing his parents from Sarawak to Kuala Lumpur a day after the incident.
The officer was attacked by a foreign man armed with a machete at a residential premises in Desa Aman Puri, Kepong, on November 11. His right wrist was successfully reattached by a team of specialists at HKL the following day in an operation lasting about eight hours.
The incident drew the attention of the Prime Minister, who condemned the attack and called for firm action against criminal acts, regardless of the perpetrators, to uphold the rule of law and ensure the safety of enforcement personnel on duty. — Bernama

Title: Two women lose RM1.18m to phone scammers posing as police
Article:
BATU PAHAT, Nov 17 — Two women in Batu Pahat and Kuala Terengganu suffered combined losses of over RM1.18 million after being duped by phone scammers posing as police officers.
In Batu Pahat, a secondary school teacher suffered losses amounting to RM748,326.50 after falling victim to a phone scam involving a suspect posing as a Bukit Aman police officer.
Batu Pahat district police chief ACP Shahrulanuar Mushaddat Abdullah Sani said the 54-year-old woman received a call in late August from an unidentified individual claiming to be from a hospital in Rawang, Selangor.
He said during the phone conversation, the victim was informed that a third party had used her name to make an insurance claim before the call was transferred to the purported police officer.
“The suspect told the victim that he would help her lodge a police report online and also asked her to hand over her ATM card for an investigation by Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM).
“Out of fear, the victim followed the suspect’s instructions, including leaving her ATM card at a nasi lemak stall next to her house on September 3,” he said in a statement today.
Shahrulanuar said the victim checked her bank account last week and discovered several money transfers totalling RM673,326.50 to accounts belonging to unknown individuals.
The victim had also deposited RM75,000 into three different bank accounts on November 4, before recounting the incident to her elder sister on Sunday and realising that she had been scammed.
In a separate case, a 63-year-old retiree in Kuala Terengganu lost RM436,000 after falling victim to a phone scam with a similar modus operandi.
Kuala Terengganu district police chief ACP Azli Mohd Noor said the victim was contacted by a suspect posing as a police officer in early October, claiming that she was involved in money laundering activities and her bank account had been blacklisted by BNM for further investigation.
“The suspect instructed the victim to pawn her jewellery and deposit the money into a bank account. She was also told to leave her bank card beside a rubbish bin at a supermarket in Kuala Nerus. Fearing legal action, the victim complied with the instructions,” he said in a statement today.
Azli said the victim realised that her money was missing after obtaining a bank statement yesterday and saw withdrawals totalling RM436,036 between October 13 and November 4.
The victim lodged a police report at 1.26pm yesterday.
Both cases are being investigated under Section 420 of the Penal Code. — Bernama

Title: Court of Appeal lets Kluang animal group pursue challenge over council’s handling of stray dogs
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Nov 17 — The Court of Appeal today granted leave to Kluang Animal Protection Association to commence judicial review seeking a declaration that the Kluang Municipal Council (MPK) had breached the Ministry of Urban Wellbeing, Housing and Local Government Secretary-General’s standard operating procedures (SOPs) in handling stray dogs within its vicinity.
A three-man bench comprising Justices Datuk Dr Shahnaz Sulaiman, Datuk Amarjeet Singh and Alice Loke Yee Ching granted leave in respect of two remedies sought by the association, namely a certiorari order and declaratory reliefs.
However, the court declined to grant leave for the association to pursue other remedies sought, namely a mandamus order, damages and a prohibitory order.
Delivering the unanimous decision, Justice Shahnaz said there is an arguable case for certiorari and declaratory relief sought, which ought to be ventilated at the substantive hearing.
“We allow in part this appeal. We grant leave for the relief of certiorari and declaration to proceed at the substantive stage,” said Justice Shahnaz.
Justice Shahnaz also said the association’s judicial review application, filed on May 7 last year, had been submitted within the prescribed time limit.
The panel remitted the case to the Johor Bahru High Court for the substantive judicial review application to be heard by a different judge or Judicial Commissioner. Case management was fixed for November 24.
The association had filed the judicial review application against MPK and its president, seeking declarations that the council had breached the SOPs issued by the ministry’s secretary-general on the capture and disposal of stray dogs in the municipality.
MPK denied allegations of mistreatment, maintaining that the dogs had been disposed of in accordance with the SOPs.
On July 21 last year, the High Court dismissed the association’s application for leave to commence the judicial review proceedings.
At the Court of Appeal proceeding today, lawyers Gavin Jayapal and Parveena Kaur represented the association while Senior Federal Counsel Suhana Sabil appeared for the Attorney-General. — Bernama

Title: French President Macron departs Malaysia after two-day official visit
Article:
SEPANG, Nov 17 — French President Emmanuel Macron departed Malaysia today after concluding his two-day official visit, which was made at the invitation of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
The visit was Macron’s first to Malaysia since he assumed office in May 2017.
The special aircraft carrying Macron, his wife Brigitte Macron and their delegation took off from the Bunga Raya Complex (BRC) at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) at 6.05pm.
Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo was present to bid farewell to Macron and his delegation.
Earlier, Macron inspected a guard of honour mounted by 28 officers and personnel from the First Battalion of the Royal Ranger Regiment, led by Captain Luqman Hakim Abd Khar.
A cultural performance by the National Department for Culture and Arts (JKKN) arts troupe was also held to mark Macron’s departure, showcasing Malaysia’s multicultural heritage through traditional dances and musical performances featuring traditional instruments.
Earlier today, Macron was accorded an official welcome at the Sultan Abdul Samad Building before holding bilateral talks with Anwar, focusing on elevating Malaysia-France relations to a Strategic Partnership, and reflecting the growing depth and strategic significance of the longstanding ties between the two countries.
In 2025, total trade between Malaysia and France amounted to RM17.78 billion (US$4.17 billion).
Malaysia’s exports to France were valued at RM6.05 billion (US$1.41 billion), with electrical and electronic products constituting the principal export category.
Imports from France totalled RM11.73 billion (US$2.76 billion), comprising mainly transport equipment, machinery and chemicals.
France is Malaysia’s 21st-largest trading partner globally and its fourth-largest trading partner among European countries. — Bernama

Title: Selangor weighs stricter rules for chicken slaughterhouses, may require certified halal slaughterers
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Nov 17 — The Selangor state government is formulating a stricter policy to improve enforcement and coordination at commercial chicken slaughterhouses, including a proposal requiring licensed premises to employ at least one certified halal slaughterer.
State Islamic Religious Affairs and Innovation Culture Committee chairman Mohammad Fahmi Ngah said the move was aimed at ensuring compliance with halal slaughtering standards and maintaining the quality of the state’s food supply.
He said 60 slaughterhouses in Selangor were licensed by local authorities (PBT), while another 149 had certified halal slaughterers but no PBT licences.
“At present, the management is somewhat fragmented, as licensing matters fall under the PBT, while halal slaughtering matters are under the Selangor Islamic Religious Department (JAIS),” he told a press conference at the Selangor State Legislative Assembly (DUN) building here today.
Mohammad Fahmi said inspections by local authorities had identified five slaughterhouses in Subang Jaya and Kuala Langat that had neither operating licences nor certified halal slaughterers. Enforcement action, including seizures, had been taken against the premises.
He said the action was necessary to ensure that chicken supplied to Selangor residents was clean and halal.
“I was also surprised that the figure was low. However, I do not think this is a major problem that should cause public concern.
“As I mentioned earlier, Selangor consumes an average of 500,000 chickens daily. Only 57 per cent of the live chickens required are produced in the state, with the rest brought in from other states for slaughter here.
“I know the public is concerned and we agree that enforcement action is necessary,” he said.
Mohammad Fahmi was previously reported as saying that the Selangor State Executive Council (MMKN) had directed local authorities to take immediate enforcement action against operators of unlicensed chicken slaughterhouses. — Bernama

Title: Govt open to proposal to expand scope of Pan Borneo Highway probe, says deputy minister
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Nov 17 — The government supports the proposal to expand the scope of the Public Accounts Committee’s (PAC) investigation into the implementation of the Sabah Pan Borneo Highway project, said Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Sabah and Sarawak) Datuk Mustapha Sakmud.
He said the government was always open to such proposals, as the findings of the PAC investigation could subsequently be presented in Parliament for collective scrutiny.
“The government is open to any necessary proposals, including the PAC’s proposal to conduct an investigation. Many of the things being done are good for the country.
“If there are problems, the PAC can look into them and present its findings in Parliament for us to assess together,” he told reporters after moderating a forum held in conjunction with the Putrajaya Festival of Ideas (Putrajaya FOI) here today.
He was commenting on plans by seven Gabungan Rakyat Sabah (GRS) Members of Parliament (MPs) to submit a memorandum to the PAC next week, seeking an expansion of the scope of its investigation into the Sabah Pan Borneo Highway project.
This includes examining the rationale and implications of the decision to terminate the Project Delivery Partner (PDP) model in 2019.
Papar MP Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali said the move was important to ensure that the PAC investigation focused not only on the project’s current status and performance, but also on previous policy decisions which were alleged to have affected the implementation timeline, contractor appointments and increases in construction costs.
On the organisation of the Putrajaya FOI, Mustapha proposed that the event be expanded to all universities and Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) institutions.
“We want to enlighten and expose our university students and other students to these new technologies.
“We want to prepare them for the future. What is important is for them to have the knowledge and basic understanding, as well as the interest and ability to prepare themselves to face future challenges,” he said.
He said early and continuous exposure was crucial to developing local capabilities and talent, ensuring that students at higher education institutions (IPTs) were prepared to face future technological challenges.
The third edition of Putrajaya FOI 2026 is being held from November 17 to 19 at the Putrajaya International Convention Centre (PICC), with the aim of positioning Malaysia as a hub for higher education and research, while elevating the culture of knowledge as a foundation for national progress.
Themed ‘Malaysia Masa Hadapan: Menggagas Teknologi, Mengangkat Insani’ (Reimagined Malaysia: Advancing Technology, Elevating Humanity), the festival was officiated by Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi and brought together academics, policymakers, industry players and the public to discuss the country’s direction in navigating future changes. — Bernama

Title: Former deputy minister Mashitah Ibrahim settles defamation suit over claims linking her to Myanmar human trafficking
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 17 — A defamation suit filed by former Deputy Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department Datuk Dr Mashitah Ibrahim against a non-governmental organisation (NGO) and two individuals over claims of human trafficking in Myanmar was resolved after all defendants issued an apology at the Shah Alam High Court yesterday.
The settlement was reached after the Malaysian International Humanitarian Organisation (MHO), its secretary-general Datuk Hishamuddin Hashim and committee member Azirul Syafiq Sazali, the first to third defendants, agreed to apologise and pay RM100,000 in costs to Mashitah.
Mashitah’s lawyer Datuk Akberdin Abdul Kadir confirmed that the consent judgment was recorded before Judicial Commissioner Datuk Anita Harun yesterday.
In yesterday’s proceedings, the three defendants were represented by lawyers Nur Fazrin Ahmad and Muhammad Falaq Adnan.
The defendants apologised to Mashitah and her husband, Datuk Abdul Shakor Abu Bakar, for their error in referring to several statements defaming and damaging the couple’s reputation, published by Justice For Myanmar, Irrawaddy Post and Scoop.com, as well as a report by the United States Institute of Peace linking Mashitah to human trafficking and migrant smuggling.
Additionally, all three defendants expressed regret over what had happened and agreed and undertook not to issue any statement concerning the case or any allegations related to the plaintiff in the future, as well as to withdraw their counterclaim against the plaintiff without costs.
On September 9, 2024, the former Baling MP filed the suit in a personal capacity, alleging that Hishamuddin uploaded, published and disseminated a video of a media statement with the caption
“Sidang Media Berkaitan Aduan Penglibatan Ahli Politik Malaysia Di Dalam Sindiket Pemerdagangan Manusia Berpusat Di Myanmar”
(Media Conference on Complaints of Malaysian Politicians’ Involvement in Human Trafficking Syndicates Based in Myanmar), made by the three defendants through the Facebook account “Hishamuddin Hashim” on August 28, 2024.
According to Mashitah, the defamatory statement implied that she and her husband were directly linked to a company called Dongmei Group, which is allegedly involved in criminal activities including human trafficking, gambling and drugs in Myanmar and internationally.
The plaintiff said the defamatory statements damaged her reputation, dignity and status as a well-known figure, senior politician and businesswoman respected by the local and international community. — Bernama

Title: Couple charged over unlicensed Dinar Dirham investment scheme
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Nov 17 — A married couple faced charges in the Sessions Court here today with accepting public deposits through an unlicensed Dinar Dirham investment scheme between 2016 and 2017.
Datuk Muhd Azrainuddin Zainal, 45, and his wife, Datin Nur Ezdiani Baharoddin, 44, each pleaded not guilty to two charges read separately before Judge Awang Kerisnada Awang Mahmud.
The first charge alleges that both accused agreed to accept such deposits via the scheme, which involved the purchase and handling of DinarCoin, without a licence at a premises in Prima SG2, Prima Sri Gombak, Batu Caves, between June and December 2016.
They are also accused of committing the same offence at a premises in Lorong Perusahaan Ringan 1, Kawasan Perusahaan Ringan, Sri Gombak, between January and November 2017.
The offences are alleged to have been committed without a licence granted under Section 10 of the Financial Services Act 2013, under Subsection 137(1) of the same Act.
If convicted, the couple faces a maximum of 10 years’ imprisonment or a fine of up to RM50 million, or both.
Earlier, Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) deputy public prosecutor Nurdeenie Abdul Rashid proposed bail of RM50,000 for each accused, with the additional condition that their passports be surrendered to the court.
However, their lawyer Mohammed Fudhail Ahmad Zulaini sought a reduction on the grounds that his clients are supporting five children aged between six and 18, and had cooperated well with the authorities throughout the investigation.
The court allowed each accused to be released on RM30,000 bail with one surety, on the condition that their passports be surrendered to the court and that they must not interfere with the prosecution witnesses.
The case is fixed for mention on January 20 next year. — Bernama

Title: ‘Students must receive royalties’: DPM Zahid calls for fair share from university innovations
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Nov 17 — Students who assist lecturers in developing innovations, including prototypes with commercial potential, should receive royalties in recognition of their contributions and efforts.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the contributions of students directly involved in the research and development of a product should be recognised alongside those of the lecturers leading the innovation.
“Do not forget that the people helping the lecturers are students who also contribute to the work.
“Students must receive royalties. It should not be just the lecturers who benefit. Students must also receive their share because they have worked equally hard,” he said when officiating the Putrajaya Festival of Ideas 2026 here today.
Ahmad Zahid said universities should also establish clear pathways for promising ideas, from prototype development and patent applications to industry adoption or commercialisation.
He said universities and the Higher Education Ministry should provide networks, funding and implementation partners to ensure researchers were not left to pursue their work on their own after making a discovery.
He said lecturers and researchers should also receive continued support following their discoveries, including greater opportunities for career development and promotion.
Ahmad Zahid said Malaysia must also dare to set ambitious goals to produce discoveries capable of changing the world while ensuring that the benefits of technological and innovation advancements were enjoyed by the people.
He said the success of research and innovation should not be measured solely by academic achievements, but also by the tangible benefits they brought to society, including farmers seeking to increase agricultural yields, young people looking for quality jobs and families striving for a better life.
“That is where the greatness of technology finds its human meaning. If every major transformation in civilisation begins with the power of human thought, let the ideas emerging from the Putrajaya Festival of Ideas be the starting point for Malaysia’s next great leap,” he said.
He also stressed that universities should be open spaces for testing ideas and debating different perspectives, while nurturing students who are willing to think critically.
Students, he said, should not rely solely on memorisation or accept views without question, but must have the courage to ask questions, construct arguments and offer solutions. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia seeks closer Asean-India cooperation against cross-border scams
Article:
MANILA, Nov 17 — Malaysia has called for stronger Asean-India cooperation in cybersecurity and combating cross-border fraud and scams to build a secure and trusted digital ecosystem, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.
“Closer intelligence sharing, capacity building, and regulatory coordination will help foster a secure, resilient, and trusted digital ecosystem,” he said in Malaysia’s national intervention at the 23rd Asean-India Summit here today.
Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan delivered the statement on behalf of Anwar, who had returned to Kuala Lumpur to receive French President Emmanuel Macron during his official visit to Malaysia.
Anwar outlined four priorities; digital connectivity, maritime cooperation, economic resilience and disaster management, as Asean and India advance the implementation of their Plan of Action 2026-2030.
He said their Comprehensive Strategic Partnership offered opportunities for closer cooperation and shared prosperity, while calling for deeper synergies between India’s policy towards the region and the Asean Outlook on the Indo-Pacific.
On maritime cooperation, the Prime Minister said Malaysia supported continued collaboration in naval exercises, disaster response, the blue economy and maritime security to strengthen regional preparedness and prosperity.
He also called for an early and substantive conclusion to the trade agreement review to improve market access, facilitate trade and strengthen supply chains between Asean and India.
Touching on disaster management, Anwar urged stronger cooperation in early warning systems, climate modelling and disaster tracking, including joint activities between India’s National Disaster Management Authority and the Asean Coordinating Centre for Humanitarian Assistance on disaster management (AHA Centre).
“It is imperative that we continue to reinforce multilateralism, our collective adherence to the UN Charter and international law, which is essential in sustaining a peaceful, stable, and predictable international order,” he said.
Meanwhile on Palestine, Anwar reiterated Malaysia’s call for an immediate and permanent ceasefire in Gaza, expressing appreciation for India’s support for a two-state solution and encouraging continued cooperation towards lasting peace in accordance with international law. — Bernama

Title: Anwar orders swift aid for next-of-kin of officer killed in crash near Tapah, other injured officers
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 17 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has directed that immediate assistance be provided to the next-of-kin of a police officer who died in an accident involving a Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) van in Sungkai, Perak, today, as well as to other officers injured in the incident.
In a Facebook post, Anwar said he has instructed his political secretary, Kamil Munim, to deliver contributions to the family of the late Muhammad Shahrul Aliff Yaacob and to the other police officers involved.
He also expressed his condolences to the family of the deceased, praying that they be granted strength and fortitude in facing this loss, and wished for a speedy recovery for the injured officers.
“My condolences to the family of the late Muhammad Shahrul Aliff Yaacob, a police officer who lost his life in an accident involving a police van in Sungkai, Perak, today.
“May his family be granted strength and fortitude in facing this loss, and may the injured police officers have a speedy recovery. Al-Fatihah,” he said.
In the incident, one police officer died and 10 others were injured after the PDRM van they were travelling in skidded and crashed into a metal guardrail at KM352 of the North-South Expressway (southbound), near Tapah, today. — Bernama

Title: Officer dies, 10 others injured after police van crashes near Tapah
Article:
IPOH, Nov 17 — A policeman was killed while 10 others were injured after a police van skidded and crashed into a metal barrier at KM352 of the North-South Expressway southbound, near Tapah, today.
Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the incident occurred at about 11.35am when the Maxus van, driven by a police personnel member and carrying 10 passengers, was travelling from the Perak police contingent headquarters to Melaka.
He said preliminary investigations found that the van’s left rear tyre was believed to have burst upon reaching the scene, causing the vehicle to go out of control before crashing into the metal barrier along the highway median.
“As a result of the accident, several passengers were thrown out of the vehicle. A 26-year-old policeman died at the scene, while four others sustained serious injuries,” he said in a statement.
Mohd Alwi said the four seriously injured victims were taken to Slim River Hospital for further treatment, while the six others who sustained minor injuries were sent to Tapah Hospital.
The body of the deceased was sent to Tapah Hospital for a post-mortem.
Members of the public with information about the incident are urged to contact the Tapah district police headquarters at 05-401 1222 or investigating traffic officer Insp Muhammad Najmuddin Zulkarnain at 017-325 6140 to assist in the investigation. — Bernama

Title: Struggling with PTPTN arrears? Borrower-Friendly Month makes loan restructuring available with minimum RM1,000 payment
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 17 — The National Higher Education Fund Corporation (PTPTN) is offering advisory services and loan restructuring facilities to borrowers through the 2026 PTPTN Borrower-Friendly Month.
In a statement today, PTPTN said the initiative, running from November 1 to December 15, allows borrowers to seek advice and arrange loan repayments according to their respective financial means.
Borrowers, particularly those with repayment arrears, are encouraged to consult PTPTN under the Education Sustainability Campaign to identify suitable repayment methods.
“PTPTN is offering payments as low as 20 per cent or RM1,000 of the total arrears, whichever is higher, for loan restructuring, loan consolidation and
Ujrah
conversion,” the statement read.
The statement said operating hours at state and branch PTPTN office counters will be extended from December 1 to 15, running from 8.30am to 6pm.
This covers all states except Terengganu, Kedah, Kelantan and Sabah, which operate from Sunday to Thursday.
Selected state and branch PTPTN office counters will be open on December 5 and 12, from 9am to 5pm.
PTPTN is also running the #PTPTNSediaBantu initiative, offering various service channels to make it easier for borrowers to conduct their transactions conveniently, quickly and securely.
“PTPTN urges all borrowers to take advantage of the opportunities available throughout the 2026 Borrower-Friendly Month.
“Committing to repay loans is not merely about discharging a responsibility; it is a meaningful one that ensures the continuity of higher education financing for the benefit of future generations,” the statement read.
For further information, borrowers can visit the corporation’s official portal at [www.ptptn.gov.my](http://www.ptptn.gov.my/). — Bernama

Title: Two years after GISBH care home raids, Selangor exco says 124 children linked to group are back in school
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Nov 17 — A total of 124 children previously linked to Global Ikhwan Services and Business Holdings (GISBH) have been registered for schooling as part of rehabilitation efforts, the Selangor State Legislative Assembly was told.
State Women and Social Welfare Development Committee chairman Anfaal Saari said other rehabilitation initiatives included the NURANI (Nilai Unggul, Rohani dan Akhlak Nadi Insan) Advocacy programme, which involved 65 participants.
“From the welfare aspect, 64 families of children who met the eligibility criteria were also provided with appropriate welfare assistance, including general assistance, child assistance, and assistance related to Persons with Disabilities (OKU),” she said.
She was replying to a question from Lim Yi Wei (PH-Kampung Tunku), who wanted to know the status of the rehabilitation of GISBH children in terms of welfare and reintegration into society.
Anfaal said all the initiatives implemented by the Selangor Social Welfare Department (JKM) placed emphasis on personal development, character-building and awareness of children’s rights and protection.
“To ensure the continued welfare and protection of these children, Selangor JKM conducts continuous monitoring and supervision through physical visits and online monitoring by child protection officers,” she said.
Meanwhile, Anfaal said state JKM had also ordered the closure of 10 premises identified as operating as care centres following inspections of 29 welfare homes linked to GISBH across Selangor.
“Of the 10 premises, three registered care centres were issued closure orders under Section 15(1) of the Care Centres Act 1993, while enforcement action under Section 16A of the same Act was taken against seven unregistered care centres.
“To date, all 10 care centres subjected to enforcement action have been closed and are no longer in operation,” she said. — Bernama

Title: Floodwaters swamp road leading to Kemuning Toll Plaza (VIDEO)
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Nov 17 — Heavy rain triggered flash flooding near the Kemuning Toll Plaza this afternoon, leaving a key route towards Klang partially submerged and causing significant traffic congestion.
According to
Kosmo
, video circulating on social media showed floodwaters covering part of the roadway leading to the toll plaza, with a queue of heavy vehicles including lorries and tankers forced to slow down as they navigated the affected stretch.
Several motorists were seen exercising caution while passing through the area, where water levels appeared high enough to cover portions of vehicle tyres.
