Title: Macron gets a taste of KL as Anwar takes him around Petaling Street and Pasar Seni
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 17 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today took President Emmanuel Macron on an informal visit to the area around Petaling Street here, in conjunction with the French leader’s official visit to Malaysia.
The two leaders arrived in the area near Chinatown at about 2pm, accompanied by delegations and senior government officials from both countries, as well as security personnel.
Also present was Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and French President Emmanuel Macron take a 30-minute stroll around Kuala Lumpur’s iconic Pasar Seni and Petaling Street as part of the French leader’s official visit to Malaysia today. — Bernama pic
During the approximately 30-minute visit, Anwar and Macron walked along the rows of shops to observe business activities and take in the atmosphere of the popular tourist destination.
They also visited the Guan Di Temple and Sri Maha Mariamman Devasthanam Temple, two historic places of worship located close to each other along Jalan Tun H.S. Lee.
French President Emmanuel Macron is welcomed with a flower garland during a visit to Sri Maha Mariamman Temple near Petaling Street with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim in Kuala Lumpur, November 17, 2026. — Bernama pic
Anwar was seen explaining to Macron the area’s unique cultural diversity, local products and the history of the historic commercial district.
The two leaders also took the opportunity to wave and mingle with members of the public and foreign tourists in the vicinity.
The visit was among the activities lined up during Macron’s official visit to Malaysia to strengthen diplomatic ties and bilateral cooperation between the two countries.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim accompanies French President Emmanuel Macron on a 30-minute walk around Pasar Seni and Petaling Street in Kuala Lumpur during the French leader’s official visit to Malaysia, November 17, 2026. — Bernama pic
It was Macron’s first official visit to Malaysia since he assumed office in May 2017.
France is Malaysia’s 10th-largest trading partner and the third-largest among European Union member states, with bilateral trade totalling €4.7 billion (approximately RM21.23 billion) in 2025, an increase of 11 per cent compared with 2024. — Bernama

Title: Melaka exco to include representatives from all BN and Perikatan parties, says Ab Rauf
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 17 — The new line-up of the Melaka State Executive Council (Exco) will comprise representatives from all component parties of Barisan Nasional (BN) and Perikatan Nasional (PN), said Chief Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ab Rauf Yusoh.
He said the Exco members would be appointed based on their capabilities to shoulder the responsibilities entrusted to them.
He said the state needed a team with a competitive edge and creative thinking to jointly take Melaka to greater heights.
“Certainly, all parties will be represented in the new Exco line-up, which is expected to be announced soon.
“I will form the best possible team to work with me in developing Melaka, with the support of all civil servants and government agencies in carrying out the responsibilities entrusted to us by the people,” he told reporters at the Chief Minister’s Office at Seri Negeri here today.
He was speaking after clocking in to begin his first day of official duties as the 13th Melaka Chief Minister. He was welcomed by State Secretary Datuk Salhah Salleh.
Ab Rauf said the team would listen to every voice, suggestion, opinion and grievance from the people, whether relating to administration, community matters or public needs, and take appropriate action, with the feedback also serving as a basis for future improvements to state government policies.
He said the state government would begin implementing 113 initiatives under the six manifesto thrusts offered by BN and PN during the 16th Melaka State Election within the first 100 days after the Exco line-up was appointed.
He said the manifesto would also serve as a guideline for each state Exco member to ensure that every promise made to the people was fulfilled according to the stipulated schedule.
He said civil servants in Melaka had also been urged to assist in implementing the manifesto initiatives to ensure that all government plans and policies were carried out and delivered comprehensively to the people.
The BN-PN pact formed the state government after winning 24 of the 28 seats contested in the state election last Saturday. — Bernama

Title: Education Ministry allocates over RM13b to tackle dilapidated schools nationwide through 2027
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 17 — The Ministry of Education has allocated over RM13 billion to address the issue of dilapidated schools nationwide through the implementation of school building reconstruction projects between 2023 and 2027, the Dewan Rakyat was told today.
Deputy Education Minister Wong Kah Woh said the allocation comprised RM1.7 billion in 2023, RM1.8 billion (2024), RM4.1 billion (2025), RM1.3 billion (2026) and RM4.1 billion for next year.
He said the allocation reflected the government’s continued efforts to address the issue of dilapidated schools and ensure that educational facilities remained safe and conducive for learning.
“This demonstrates the Madani Government’s commitment to ensuring that issues of schools with dilapidated buildings are dealt with,” he said during the minister’s question-and-answer session in Dewan Rakyat today.
Wong said the government has also implemented the Renovation and Upgrading (USNT) initiative as a supplement to existing maintenance allocations, with RM100 million set aside this year for schools in Peninsular Malaysia.
The condition of school buildings is monitored by the District Education Office (PPD) and State Education Department (JPN), while the Public Works Department is also involved in technical assessments and making recommendations on demolition and reconstruction.
“If a building has been classified under Scale Six, major maintenance work will be carried out to prevent it from being classified under Scale Seven,” he added.
He said this when replying to a supplementary question from Salamiah Mohd Nor (PN-Temerloh) regarding the MOE’s prioritisation policy, mechanisms for periodic monitoring of dilapidated school buildings and the allocations provided by the government to address the issue.
Meanwhile, in response to a question from Datuk Seri Panglima Madius Tangau (PH-Tuaran) about the timeline to replace buildings categorised under Scale Seven at Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaaan (SMK) Tamparuli and SMK Tenghilan in Sabah, Wong said the MOE had drawn up a three-phase plan involving short-, medium- and long-term measures to address the issue.
He said that, as an immediate measure, buildings identified as high-risk at both schools had been vacated, while USNT projects and maintenance works were being carried out to ensure the safety of students and school personnel.
The MOE also plans to construct classrooms using the modular Industrialised Building System (IBS) under Rolling Plan (RP) 2 of the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP), involving 14 classrooms at SMK Tenghilan and between 14 and 16 classrooms at SMK Tamparuli, with preliminary works targeted to begin in February 2027 and construction expected to take between six and nine months.
“For the long-term solution, the MOE is finalising the implementation of a Structural Integrity Test (SIT) with Sabah JKR before submitting a request for funding for the reconstruction of academic buildings under RP3 of the 13th Malaysia Plan in 2028,” he added.
He said the MOE was prepared to provide the necessary allocation for the SIT, with the cost for SMK Tenghilan estimated at RM400,000 to ensure the assessment could be carried out as soon as possible. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia backs petroleum stockpiling for regional energy security, but says it must be voluntary
Article:
MANILA, Nov 17 — Malaysia recognises the value of petroleum stockpiling in strengthening regional energy resilience, but any arrangement should be voluntary and commercially based, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
“Nevertheless, any such arrangement should be pursued on a voluntary and commercial basis, taking into account each member state’s national circumstances, priorities, and domestic readiness,” he said in Malaysia’s national intervention at the Asia Zero Emission Community (Azec) Leaders’ Meeting here today.
Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan delivered the statement on behalf of Anwar, who had returned to Kuala Lumpur to receive French President Emmanuel Macron, who is on an official visit to Malaysia.
Anwar reaffirmed Malaysia’s commitment to ensuring that decarbonisation proceeded alongside economic growth and energy security.
He said Malaysia remained steadfast in its target of achieving net-zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050, with the National Energy Transition Roadmap providing a clear and pragmatic pathway for the transition.
The Prime Minister said carbon capture, utilisation and storage (CCUS) was central to Malaysia’s decarbonisation strategy, with the country strategically positioned to serve as a regional hub.
He also reaffirmed Malaysia’s commitment to advancing the Asean Power Grid.
“Enhancing cross-border power interconnection is critical to maximising the regional utilisation of renewable energy, optimising grid stability, and fostering sub-regional energy trade,” he said.
Anwar said Malaysia stood ready to contribute as a reliable partner, a green investment destination and an active contributor to regional climate solutions.
“We look forward to working closely with all member states to turn our shared vision into tangible outcomes,” he said. — Bernama

Title: MCMC appoints TM to build RM2.7b undersea cable linking Peninsular Malaysia to Sabah, Sarawak
Article:
CYBERJAYA, Nov 17 — The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) has appointed TM Technology Services Sdn. Sdn Bhd (TM) as the universal service provider for designing, implementing, and operating the Madani Submarine Cable Connection System (SALAM) worth RM2.7 billion.
It said in a statement that the project will be funded through the Universal Service Provision (USP) Fund, which means the SALAM system will enhance communication connection capacity between Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah and Sarawak.
“It simultaneously supports the provision of more reliable digital services to the community, businesses and government. In addition, it will also provide an alternative route for data traffic, thereby reducing the risk of service disruption in the event the existing undersea cables experience interference or damage,” said MCMC.
With a length of approximately 5,500 kilometres, the system will be implemented by TM based on Alcatel Submarine Networks (ASN) submarine cable technology and will meet the increasing demand, considering that the capacity utilisation of the existing submarine cable network, which has been in operation since 2017, has now reached about 85 per cent.
According to MCMC, the SALAM system will include 10 new submarine cable landing stations, namely Cherating and Sedili in Peninsular Malaysia; Kuching, Sibu (Matu) and Bintulu (Samalaju) in Sarawak; as well as Kota Kinabalu, Kudat, Pulau Banggi, Sandakan and Tawau in Sabah.
The additional capacity will support the expansion of broadband and 5G networks, cloud services, artificial intelligence, and data centres, thereby providing a stronger foundation to expand digital opportunities, particularly in Sabah and Sarawak.
“Four pairs of optical fibre will be dedicated to meet the strategic needs of the nation, including sovereign cloud infrastructure, government digital services and cybersecurity.
“SALAM reflects MCMC’s commitment to strengthening Malaysia’s digital infrastructure so that more communities and businesses can enjoy the benefits of the digital economy,” said MCMC.
The implementation of the SALAM project is scheduled to begin in mid-December and is expected to be completed in phases by the first quarter of 2030.
Earlier, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and French President Emmanuel Macron witnessed the exchange of a memorandum of understanding between TM and ASN at the Sultan Abdul Samad Building in Kuala Lumpur. — Bernama

Title: France, Malaysia strike ‘unique’ rare earth deal as defence ties deepen
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 17 — France and Malaysia agreed today to deepen ties in the lucrative field of rare earth minerals and in defence, with visiting President Emmanuel Macron hailing a “new milestone” in relations.
Macron, who is on a two-day whistle-stop tour of the Southeast Asian nation, told a news conference that a joint rare earths project will include “the option for refining in France” — a “unique” agreement, according to Malaysia’s Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim.
Malaysia plays a major role in rare earth processing, courted by many countries as an important option outside China, which holds a monopoly on critical minerals used in products ranging from smartphones to fighter jets, electric cars and wind turbines.
The country already hosts the largest rare earths processing plant outside of China, and the planned project between French firm Carester and Malaysia’s Malaco Mining would add another 13,000 tonnes of processed minerals, including those needed for high-performance magnets.
Macron said the joint project was set for an operational launch early next year.
It will “not only encompass extraction, but also local processing of reserved volumes and capacities, including the option for refining in France, which was a key element for our entire value chain,” Macron said.
Anwar said that “we have done something which is unique”, adding: “We do not export raw materials. But with France, we’ll do so because you are committed to that — processing and working with Malaysians as a team”.
Carester in July announced plans with Malaco to build a rare earths separation plant in Malaysia’s northern Perak state under a 10-year joint venture.
Macron’s visit also saw the two governments sign agreements on defence, energy supply and digital cooperation.
This included the establishment of a regional centre for “countering hybrid threats” and the provision of Airbus-built search-and-rescue helicopters to the Malaysian armed forces.
“As we approach the 70th anniversary of our diplomatic relations, our two countries are reaching a new milestone with this visit,” Macron said.
Bilateral trade between France and Malaysia reached more than 4.9 billion euros (RM22.12 billion) last year. — AFP

Title: Anwar: Malaysia keen to attract more French investment, including in rare earths
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 17 — Malaysia is seeking greater French investment in key sectors, particularly rare earth processing, as the two countries look to deepen economic ties, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said on today.
Anwar said cooperation in the rare earth sector must be built on trust, stressing Malaysia’s commitment to expanding processing activities in an environmentally safe manner.
“Rare earth processing is something we are very keen on attracting and expanding and we are doing it in an environmentally safe way,” he said.
Anwar said French investment in Malaysia continued to grow, citing aerospace, defence and semiconductors among the sectors offering opportunities for further cooperation.
Anwar said this in his opening remarks ahead of a bilateral meeting with visiting French President Emmanuel Macron at the historic Sultan Abdul Samad Building here on today.
Macron also expressed France’s interest in the rare earth sector, describing it as one of the key areas the country wanted to pursue with Malaysia through a respectful and mutually beneficial partnership.
The French president also highlighted opportunities to expand cooperation in semiconductors, artificial intelligence and data centres, alongside defence, security and economic ties.
According to a Foreign Ministry statement issued on yesterday, the visit focuses on efforts to elevate Malaysia-France relations to a Strategic Partnership, covering trade and investment, critical minerals, energy transition, defence and education.
In 2025, total trade between Malaysia and France amounted to RM17.78 billion (US$4.17 billion), with Malaysian exports valued at RM6.05 billion (US$1.41 billion), mainly comprising electrical and electronic products.
Imports from France totalled RM11.73 billion (US$2.76 billion), consisting primarily of transport equipment, machinery and chemicals.
France was Malaysia’s 21st-largest trading partner globally and fourth-largest among European countries in 2025.
On education and culture, Anwar highlighted longstanding cooperation between the two countries, including opportunities for Malaysian students to study at French universities.
“We need to continue to support the translation of Malay classics into French, as well as the translation of French classics into Malay,” he said.
Turning to international developments, Anwar welcomed France’s position on Palestine and Gaza, describing it as a voice of conscience in defence of humanity.
He also said Malaysia had taken a strong position against Russia’s war in Ukraine while maintaining relations with Moscow.
Macron, meanwhile, said both countries could strengthen their sovereignty and independence without adopting a confrontational approach towards major powers.
“There is no double standard for France.
“We are on the side of the UN Charter and we do support people’s rights, and sovereignty, and territorial integrity everywhere,” he said.
Macron also referred to the New York Declaration of July 2025 and France’s recognition of Palestine as part of its diplomatic efforts on the issue.
He said France had worked with several countries to pursue a peaceful resolution to the conflict and address the humanitarian situation in the region.
He also reaffirmed France’s support for Ukraine’s sovereignty against Russia’s aggression.
“So we are predictable in this regard and loyal to our partners,” he said.
Macron is on a two-day official visit to Malaysia beginning yesterday at Anwar’s invitation, his first visit to the country since assuming office in May 2017.
Also present at the bilateral meeting were Deputy Prime Minister and Energy Transition and Water Transformation Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof, Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani, Tourism, Arts and Culture Minister Datuk Seri Tiong King Sing, Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin and Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar. — Bernama

Title: Labuan-Sabah Bridge feasibility study complete, findings to go before council next year
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 17 — A feasibility study on the proposed Labuan-Sabah Bridge, which could connect the Federal Territory of Labuan to the Sabah Pan Borneo Highway network, was completed on November 15, with its findings set to be presented to the National Physical Planning Council (MPFN) next year, the Dewan Rakyat was told today.
Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi said the study, which began on May 16, 2025, was carried out by the Works Ministry at the request of the Federal Territories Ministry after it was approved under the Fifth Rolling Plan (RP5) of the 12th Malaysia Plan (12MP) in 2025.
He said the findings would be presented at an MPFN meeting chaired by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim for further consideration of the proposed mega project.
“The project’s implementation and financing arrangements can only be determined after the study findings have been presented to the MPFN next year,” he said when replying to a question from Datuk Dr Suhaili Abdul Rahman (Labuan) on whether the government would consider building the Labuan-Menumbok Bridge as part of the strategic Sabah Pan Borneo Highway network.
Nanta said the project would require coordination among several ministries, including the Economy Ministry, Finance Ministry and Federal Territories Ministry, with the Works Ministry responsible for the technical study.
Responding to Suhaili’s supplementary question on when construction could begin and how the project would be financed, he said the timeline could only be finalised once the project was approved by the central agencies, subject to the government’s financial position.
If built, the bridge would provide a direct connection between Labuan and Jalan Menumbok in Sabah, with a road network stretching about 70 kilometres linking it to the Pan Borneo Highway interchange in Beaufort, he said.
Meanwhile, Nanta said the government had approved RM100 million under RP4 of the 12MP to upgrade the Jalan Beaufort-Menumbok (R502), from the Binkul Roundabout to the Menumbok Ferry Terminal junction in Kuala Penyok, Sabah.
“The project includes upgrading a 1.1-km stretch of road between Sekolah Agama Negeri Menumbok and the Menumbok Ferry Terminal, along with road pavement repairs and slope improvement works at selected locations.
“The road currently serves as an important link between Sabah and Labuan through ferry services. It will also connect the Pan Borneo Highway to the proposed Labuan-Sabah Bridge,” he said, adding that the government had also approved RM22 million to upgrade the vehicle and passenger ferry terminal jetties in Labuan. — Bernama

Title: Nearly 14,000 deepfake, manipulated content items removed after MCMC requests since 2024
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 17 — A total of 13,883 image-manipulation or deepfake content items have been taken down by service providers following requests from the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC), in response to public complaints received between January 1, 2024 and October 31 this year, the Dewan Rakyat was told today.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said MCMC had also investigated 61 cases involving the misuse of artificial intelligence (AI) technology under Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998 (Act 588) between January 1 and October 31 this year, with 10 cases brought to court.
He said of the 10 cases, six have been decided by the courts, resulting in total fines of RM19,500, while the remaining four are still before the courts.
“Additionally, seven cases were offered compounds totalling RM755,000, while 17 warning letters were issued. The remaining 27 cases are either still under investigation or have been classified as requiring no further action,” he said during Question Time,
Fahmi was responding to Afnan Hamimi Taib Azamudden (PN-Alor Setar) on the government’s strategies to tackle the growing spread of deepfakes and AI-generated synthetic news impersonating leaders, institutions and individuals for fraudulent purposes and information manipulation.
The minister said the government viewed the misuse of AI technology seriously, particularly in the creation of deepfakes, identity impersonation and the spread of false information.
Enforcement action can be taken under Section 233 of Act 588 if the content meets the prescribed elements of an offence, he said.
Fahmi noted that the Online Safety Act 2025 (Act 566) also provided a regulatory framework to address harmful online content, including AI-generated material that falls within the categories covered by the law.
He said the Risk Mitigation Code (RMC), which came into force on June 1, required licensed service providers to establish mechanisms to identify, assess and address harmful content.
“The code also requires images, audio or videos generated or manipulated using AI that could be mistaken for authentic content to be clearly labelled or marked,” he said.
Fahmi said the government, through MCMC, was also conducting the Safe Internet Campaign to raise public awareness and digital literacy, particularly in identifying deepfakes, identity impersonation and AI-generated misinformation. — Bernama

Title: BN submits new Negeri Sembilan MB candidate for Tuanku Muhriz’s approval
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Nov 17 — Barisan Nasional (BN) has submitted a candidate for the post of Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar to the Yang Dipertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir for consideration and approval following Datuk Ismail Lasim’s resignation.
BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the candidate’s name was submitted to the palace yesterday.
“A letter was sent to the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan following the submission of Ismail’s resignation letter to Tuanku. I also received a copy of the same resignation letter.
“It is a normal practice for a party, particularly BN, to submit a letter proposing a new Menteri Besar candidate for Tuanku’s consideration and approval. It is entirely up to Tuanku to decide whether to approve the name I have submitted,” he told reporters when asked about the latest development concerning Ismail’s resignation last night.
The Deputy Prime Minister was met after officiating at the Putrajaya Festival of Ideas (FOI) here today. Also present was Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir, who is also BN secretary-general.
Ahmad Zahid, who is also Umno president, said the palace would announce the appointment if the candidate received the Ruler’s approval.
“As party leader and BN chairman, I leave the matter entirely to Tuanku Muhriz’s discretion and approval, as well as to the palace to make the announcement,” he said.
On Ismail’s resignation, Ahmad Zahid stressed that the party had never instructed the assemblyman to step down, saying the decision was made voluntarily.
“He did not give a reason. Perhaps he felt that he wanted the problems in Negeri Sembilan to be resolved as soon as possible,” he said.
Asked whether the appointment of a new Menteri Besar would resolve the constitutional crisis in the state, Ahmad Zahid expressed hope that the matter could be settled amicably.
Meanwhile, Negeri Sembilan Umno liaison committee chairman Datuk Seri Jalaluddin Alias expressed the state party’s appreciation for Ismail’s service and contributions during his tenure as head of the state government.
He said the state Umno leadership would give its full cooperation to the party’s top leadership to ensure the smooth running of the state administration and safeguard the people’s welfare.
“In ensuring that this process proceeds smoothly, the state Umno has confidence in the wisdom of the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, and will uphold His Royal Highness’s decree,” he told reporters after chairing a special state political bureau meeting with Perikatan Nasional assemblymen at Wisma Umno Negeri Sembilan in Seremban today.
Asked about Ismail’s absence from the meeting, Jalaluddin said the Juasseh assemblyman had been invited but might have had other matters to attend to. Several other assemblymen were also unable to attend due to prior commitments.
He said all parties should ensure the issue was resolved amicably, with prudence and in a spirit of harmony, so that the state administration could continue to function smoothly.
Last night, Zambry, in a statement, announced that Ismail had resigned as the Menteri Besar of Negeri Sembilan, and that Ahmad Zahid had also received a copy of the resignation letter, which was addressed and sent to the Yang Dipertuan Besar.
Ismail, 67, was sworn in as Menteri Besar on August 2. — Bernama

Title: Russia and Ukraine trade bridge strikes ahead of Xi-Trump-Putin talks
Article:
KYIV, Nov 17 — Russia hit two major bridges in Kyiv while Ukraine struck Moscow’s link to annexed Crimea for the second night in a row, officials said Tuesday, ahead of a historic meeting of Chinese, US and Russian leaders.
Russia’s defence ministry said it downed 1,441 Ukrainian drones in a major overnight barrage, with Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin reporting that more than 300 of them were headed to the capital itself.
Ukraine’s Volodymyr Zelensky had warned of major attacks in the days leading up to a meeting in China’s Shenzhen on Thursday between presidents Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin.
US President Trump said the fighting in Ukraine would be among the topics canvassed in the talks, which come at a time of renewed diplomatic activity to find a path to end almost five years of war.
European officials on Monday also joined discussions with Ukrainian and US negotiators on ways to draw Russia into “direct engagement” on ending its invasion, launched in February 2022.
Fighting did not let up with Russia striking two major bridges in Kyiv late Monday, during attacks that disrupted heating and water in parts of the capital, Mayor Vitali Klitschko posted on Telegram.
City authorities said both bridges were closed to traffic.
For the second day in a row, Ukrainian forces hit the symbolic bridge that links the annexed Crimean peninsula to Russia, according to a Moscow-installed official.
“The enemy has attacked the Crimean Bridge again. At the moment, traffic is suspended,” Sergei Aksyonov, the Russian-installed governor of Crimea, posted on Telegram on Tuesday.
Traffic had been halted on the bridge for almost 17 hours from 23:54 (2054 GMT) on Monday following a previous attack, according to the road traffic authority.
Zelensky had cautioned on Monday that Russia was preparing to strike and vowed Ukraine was ready to respond to “every one of their evils”.
European involvement
The United States has in recent weeks renewed a push for an end to the conflict but diplomatic efforts have so far failed to reach a breakthrough, with fighting grinding into another winter.
Previously, talks on settling Europe’s worst conflict since World War II have been held in the Ukraine-Russia-US format, with Moscow wanting to keep the Europeans out of discussions.
However, Zelensky said on Monday that representatives from France, Britain, Germany, Poland, Italy and the European Union joined an online meeting with US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner.
The Ukrainian president described the European attendees as “those who will represent it in negotiations with the Russians”.
Kushner confirmed the talks, which he said included national security advisers from the European nations as well as EU and Nato officials.
He insisted that “progress” was being made to end the war.
Much of the focus of the discussions, Kushner said, had been on ways to “facilitate direct engagement” between Ukraine and Russia.
US media outlet Axios reported that Witkoff and Kushner planned to take part in a meeting of European and Ukrainian officials set for Thursday — the same day as the Shenzhen trilateral meeting.
‘Safeguarding world peace’
Zelensky has raised alarm that the talks between the leaders of Russia, China and the United States on the sidelines of a regional summit could be a Yalta-like “redistribution of spheres of influence” for the 21st century.
The Yalta summit of 1945 saw US president Franklin D. Roosevelt, Britain’s Winston Churchill and Soviet leader Joseph Stalin carve up new post-WWII territorial boundaries with little concern for other countries.
Ukraine’s Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiha said the presidents’ meeting would “only encourage Putin to continue this war”.
A Kremlin spokesperson pushed back on those contentions, saying that “all comparisons with Yalta are political science exercises that have nothing to do with reality.”
“To say that someone is getting together to ‘decide the fate of the world’ — that is certainly not Russia and certainly not China,” the spokesperson added in the comments carried by Russian state media.
China has not provided specific details on the topics of discussion beyond “safeguarding world peace” and “promoting strategic stability in major power relations”.
The White House had earlier signalled the Ukraine war was not expected to be addressed -- before Trump said on Monday that it would be.
“We’ll talk about my favourite subject, Ukraine,” Trump told reporters. — AFP

Title: Umno Negeri Sembilan not informed of Ismail Lasim’s resignation plan, says Jalaluddin
Article:
SEREMBAN, Nov 17 — Umno Negeri Sembilan was not informed directly by Datuk Ismail Lasim about his intention to resign as Menteri Besar, according to the state party chairman, Datuk Seri Jalaluddin Alias.
Speaking after a special meeting at the Umno Negeri Sembilan headquarters today, Jalaluddin said the party only learned of the matter through Umno’s national leadership.
According to
Berita Harian
, the Juasseh assemblyman, who also serves as deputy chairman of Umno Negeri Sembilan, did not personally notify the state leadership of his decision, he added.
“I was only informed by the party’s top leadership of the Menteri Besar’s intention to resign. He did not personally inform Umno Negeri Sembilan,” Jalaluddin told reporters.
The special meeting was also attended by state assemblymen from Perikatan Nasional (PN).
On Monday, Barisan Nasional secretary-general Dr Zambry Abd Kadir announced that Ismail Lasim had submitted a resignation letter dated November 16 to the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir.
A copy of the letter was also received by BN chairman and Umno president Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.
Asked about claims that Ismail had been pressured into stepping down, Jalaluddin declined to comment, saying the priority was to ensure the state government continued to function smoothly and that the transition process proceeded without disruption. He also refrained from commenting on a statement from the Negeri Sembilan palace, which has yet to verify the authenticity of the resignation letter.
Jalaluddin, who is also the Member of Parliament for Jelebu, said the state Umno leadership respected Ismail’s decision and expressed appreciation for his service and contributions during his tenure as Menteri Besar.
He said Umno Negeri Sembilan would continue to cooperate fully with the party’s central leadership to ensure stable governance and safeguard the welfare of the people. The party would also respect the wisdom and decisions of Tuanku Muhriz as the process unfolds.
“We call on all parties to remain calm and respect the ongoing process. In any situation, the interests of the people must remain the priority,” he said, expressing confidence that the current political and administrative uncertainty in the state could be resolved amicably.
Regarding a possible successor to Ismail, Jalaluddin said any appointment would depend on recommendations from the party’s top leadership and the consent of Tuanku Muhriz.

Title: ‘Don’t make others the scapegoat’: Ismail Lasim’s son questions statement on father’s resignation
Article:
SEREMBAN, Nov 17 — The son of Negeri Sembilan Mentri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim has questioned a statement issued by another party concerning his father’s resignation, including whether it was made at the party’s direction.
In an Instagram post, Naim Ismail, who uses the account @naimismaill_, appeared to suggest that someone was being made a scapegoat over the matter, Kosmo! Online reported.
“Who issued the statement saying that you wanted to resign? Did you personally make that statement? If not, on what basis did the party come forward with a media statement?” he wrote.
Naim said his father had followed all party instructions from the beginning, but expressed disappointment that matters had ended this way.
In the same post, he warned certain parties against making others scapegoats to serve their own interests.
“Before anything has even been settled, there are already efforts to bring down one of their own. Do not make someone else the scapegoat for the interests of certain parties. If you truly want to protect the party, do not let your own people be treated this way,” he said.
Naim added that everyone knew what had happened and urged those involved not to act as though only one side was at fault.
